docs.title: Tribos Documentation
docs.text:
Tribos Engineering & Scientific R&D Assistant Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

Tribos (τρίβος — "a worn path, practice, diligent inquiry") is an authoritative multi-agent scientific discovery platform for Engineering, Physics, and the Mathematical Sciences, engineered by ChronoStrider Engineering.

Tribos combines a 5-stage deterministic-and-agentic reasoning pipeline with five specialized computational engines for exact symbolic mathematics, dynamical systems simulation, sandboxed experimental data computation, physical constants & metrology, and scholarly literature synthesis.

docs.title: Specialist Agents
docs.text:
Every scientific query in Tribos is decomposed and routed to domain-specialized agents equipped with validated toolsets:

Specialist Agent Domain Role Core Tools & Key Capabilities Archivon Scientific Literature & Citations archivon_literature_search, archivon_paper_details, archivon_recommendFederated multi-source search across arXiv, zbMATH Open, Crossref, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, and NASA ADS; reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), cross-encoder reranking, claim-level citation grounding, and retraction verification. Axiom Symbolic Mathematics & Formal Verification axiom_simplify, axiom_solve, axiom_calculus, axiom_dsolve, axiom_linalg, axiom_verify_identity, axiom_latexExact computer algebra via SymPy: closed-form equation solving, calculus (differentiation, integration, limits, series), ODE dsolve, exact linear algebra, and dual symbolic/mpmath identity verification. Dynamis Dynamical Systems & Simulation dynamis_simulate_ode, dynamis_equilibrium, dynamis_parameter_scan, dynamis_optimize, dynamis_fit_parameters, dynamis_root_findSciPy numerical computing: initial value problem (IVP) integration (RK45, DOP853, Radau, BDF), fixed-point search, Jacobian eigenvalue stability classification, parameter sensitivity scans, nonlinear curve fitting, and optimization. Calcula Sandboxed Computation & Data Analysis calcula_run_python, calcula_describe_datasetIsolated subprocess Python sandbox (no network, strict memory & time limits) running NumPy, SciPy, SymPy, Pandas, Pint, Matplotlib, NetworkX, mpmath, and statsmodels; automatic dataset inspection (CSV, TSV, HDF5, MAT). Physis Physical Constants, Units & Reference physis_constants, physis_units, physis_oeis, physis_materials, physis_wolfram, physis_encyclopediaNIST CODATA 2022 fundamental physical constants, Pint unit conversions and equation dimensional homogeneity checks (\([M^a L^b T^c I^d \Theta^e N^f J^g]\)), OEIS integer sequences, Materials Project crystal data, and Wikipedia scientific definitions.

docs.title: Five Interchangeable Orchestration Frameworks
docs.text:
Tribos supports five interchangeable multi-agent orchestration frameworks configurable per-request via framework or globally with TRIBOS_DEFAULT_FRAMEWORK (with automatic query routing via auto):

  1. Plan-and-Execute (agentic-plan-execute) (API Default): Decomposes the research question, executes an LLM-planned tool DAG in parallel, performs gap-driven re-retrieval (Self-RAG), conducts counter-evidence search (PaperQA2/ContraCrow), and calculates calibrated claim confidence scores.
  2. Authoritative ReAct Compiler (authoritative-react-compiler): Structured deterministic pipeline executing parallel Stage 1 evidence gathering followed by Stage 2 numerical/symbolic computation and Reflexion auditing.
  3. Centralized Supervisor (multi-agent-supervisor): Magentic-One-style progress ledger delegating subtasks dynamically to Archivon, Axiom, Dynamis, Calcula, and Physis.
  4. Specialist Swarm (multi-agent-swarm): Peer-to-peer delegation where specialist agents directly hand off context and intermediate findings to each other until synthesis is complete.
  5. Multi-Agent Debate (multi-agent-debate): Multi-agent peer debate where mathematical, physical, and computational claims undergo rigorous cross-agent critique before finalizing the derivation.

docs.title: Derivation-First Structure & KaTeX Math Rendering
docs.text: Scientific responses emitted by Tribos adhere strictly to a derivation-first structure: - Result: Immediate, unambiguous answer to the inquiry with dimensional units. - Derivation: Step-by-step mathematical derivation formatted in LaTeX notation, rendered on the frontend via KaTeX and documented via MathJax. - Verification: Exact symbolic back-substitution, dimensional homogeneity verification (\(LHS \equiv RHS\)), or numerical simulation checks. - Assumptions & Limits: Physical regimes of validity (e.g., non-relativistic, laminar, low Reynolds number, ideal gas). - References: Inline grounded citations to preprints (arXiv:), journals (doi:), theorem databases (zbl:), or constants (nist:).

docs.title: Tribos Scientific Capability Matrix
docs.text:
Last updated: 28 October 2026

This matrix defines the supported mathematical, numerical simulation, and engineering calculation capabilities of Tribos, their underlying engines, boundaries, and validation criteria.

docs.title: 1. Supported Workloads & Numerical Engines
docs.text: Domain Method / Operation Engine / Package Supported Input Limits Validation & Oracle Circuit Dynamics Ideal RC Charging Step Response tribos.engcalc.electrical \(R > 0\), \(C > 0\), \(V_s \in \mathbb{R}\), \(t \ge 0\). Closed-form analytic solution \(v_C(t) = V_s(1 - e^{-t/\tau})\), KVL balance residual \(< 10^{-12}\). Structural Mechanics Rectangular Cantilever Tip Load tribos.engcalc.structural Linear elastic Euler-Bernoulli regime; \(L, b, h, E > 0\), \(P \in \mathbb{R}\). Exact second moment \(I = bh^3/12\), max deflection \(\delta = PL^3/(3EI)\), moment \(M = PL\), stress \(\sigma = Mc/I\). ODE Simulation Fixed-Step Runge-Kutta 4 (RK4) tribos.dynamis.engine Stated scalar or system ODEs; fixed step \(h > 0\), explicit steps \(N \le 10^5\). Grid step strictly verified (\(N+1\) points matching \(t_{\text{span}}\)); underdamped harmonic oscillator verified against closed-form within \(10^{-4}\). PDE Diffusion 1D Heat Equation (FTCS) tribos.dynamis.pde 1D bounded domain \([0, L]\), Dirichlet boundaries, diffusion \(\alpha > 0\). Stability parameter \(r = \frac{\alpha \Delta t}{\Delta x^2} \le 0.5\). Stability gate enforces \(r \le 0.5\) (unstable runs refused); boundary temperatures strictly checked at every time step and final field. Stochastic Integration Crude 1D Monte Carlo tribos.dynamis.monte_carlo Integrable 1D expressions; \(N \le 10^7\) uniform samples. PRNG via NumPy PCG64. Reproducible seed enforcement; sample variance \(s^2 \ge 0\), non-negative standard error \(SE = (b-a)s/\sqrt{N}\); reference error tracking. Exact Mathematics Symbolic Algebra, Calculus, Proofs SymPy / tribos.axiom Safe math strings parsed via parse_math / safe_parse_expr; domain restrictions \(n \ge n_0\), modular congruences \(n \equiv a \pmod m\). Exact rational / integer arithmetic; domain scoping isolation (out-of-domain inputs marked undecided, never contradicted).

docs.title: 2. Explicit Unsupported Boundaries & Limitations
docs.text:
Tribos honestly reports limitations and refuses to substitute toy approximations without notice:

  1. Arbitrary 3D CFD & Continuum Fluid Flow:
  2. Tribos does not include an arbitrary 3D Navier-Stokes Navier solver or fluid-structure grid generator.
  3. Flow computations are limited to closed-form dimensionless numbers (e.g. Reynolds number) and explicit 1D analytical relations.
  4. Arbitrary 3D Finite Element Analysis (FEA):
  5. Complex 3D CAD stress/strain meshes are not solved natively.
  6. Structural analyses are limited to verified 1D beam, shaft, bolt, and thin-walled pressure vessel engineering formulations.
  7. Stiff High-Order Stated ODE Systems without Stability Tuning:
  8. Fixed-step RK4 will diverge on stiff ODE systems (e.g. Robertson kinetics); adaptive stiff solvers (e.g. Radau/BDF) must be explicitly requested.
  9. Universal Automated Theorem Proving:
  10. Open unsolved conjectures (e.g. Erdős–Straus, Riemann Hypothesis) cannot be proved universally; Tribos verifies stated instances, parametric families, and congruence classes without asserting global resolution.

docs.title: 3. Strict Contract Validation Invariants (_contract_checks)
docs.text: Every executed simulation artifact returned to the user or orchestrator must pass deterministic contract checks: - ODE Reports: Must include complete monotonic time grid array \(t\), state trajectories matching grid length \(N+1\), endpoint matching \(t_{\text{span}}\), and initial state matching within floating-point tolerance. - Monte Carlo Reports: Integrand expression equivalence verified via SymPy safe_parse_expr(), integration bounds matched, \(SE \ge 0.0\), finite estimate, and valid sample variance. - Heat FTCS Reports: Diffusivity, \(\Delta x\), \(\Delta t\), stability ratio \(r \le 0.5\), grid points, and Dirichlet boundary constraints strictly checked at initial, intermediate, and final snapshots. - Engineering Calculators: Input parameters match within tolerance, calculator ID matches, and output fields are non-empty and finite.

docs.title: Contributing to Tribos
docs.text:
Tribos: a research partner for engineering, physics and mathematics Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Tribos. Bug reports, feature ideas, corrections and documentation improvements are all welcome. Please read this page before opening an issue or a pull request.

docs.title: Reporting bugs and requesting features
docs.text: Use the GitHub issue tracker. Check open and recently closed issues first, and follow the bug or feature template. For a wrong answer, include the question, the answer and what you expected; the conversation ID shown at the top of the chat helps us find the run and the checks it made.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
1. Work against the latest main, and open an issue first for any larger change.
  2. Read AGENTS.md for the architecture map and the conventions (tools, settings, verification, the sandbox). Every new TRIBOS_* variable is a Setting(...) in tribos/config/settings.py, and the configuration reference is regenerated with scripts/gen_env_reference.py.
  3. Keep the checks green:
uv run pytest -q                                              # offline: no network, no model calls
uv run ruff check tribos app tests scripts --select F,E9
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r tribos app --severity-level high
uv run python scripts/gen_env_reference.py --check
cd web && npm run typecheck && npx eslint src && npm test && npx next build
  1. Tests must not need the network: use the fakes in tests/fakes.py and tests/agentic_fakes.py.
  2. Never commit .env or any key.

Good first contributions are issues labelled help wanted, new deterministic tools for a domain engine (each with a precise description, a JSON schema and a test against known answers), and documentation fixes.

docs.title: Feature roadmap: tasks for AI coding agents
docs.text:
Read AGENTS.md first. It has setup, commands, architecture and conventions.

Each task below is self-contained: a goal, where it plugs in, the files to create or own, and acceptance criteria. The tasks can be done in any order and by different agents at the same time, as long as each agent edits only its task's files. The shared files are:

  • tribos/extensions/__init__.py
  • tribos/config/settings.py
  • app/backend/main.py (router list)
  • tribos/agents/stem_evidence.py
  • web/src/components/artifacts/registry.tsx

In the shared files, add small entries only. Do not restructure them.

Status (2026-10-25): all ten tasks are DONE (see each section's note), committed on the features-roadmap branch in the order T8, T1, T4, T3, T2, T9, T6, T7, T5, T10 (T2 before T9 because its work was already in progress). The end-to-end run with the live model found and fixed three integration gaps: closed computations that need a specialised tool now reach the planner, the planner is told the attached files' ids, and the calculators accept the input names a model writes. One live gap remains: the planning model does not always plan the engineering-calculator call.

Definition of done for every task:

  • New tests pass.
  • The full pytest suite stays at 0 failures.
  • ruff --select F,E9 and bandit --severity-level high are clean.
  • Web: npm run typecheck, npx eslint src (0 errors), npm test and npx next build all pass.
  • scripts/gen_env_reference.py --check passes. Run it after adding settings.

docs.title: T1: Fit ODE models to uploaded data
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Extended the existing fitter with safe ODE least squares, robust multi-start/bounds/initial-state fitting, covariance diagnostics, measurement loaders, agentic execution and fit/residual/CI cards. No dependencies added; intervals are local normal approximations, with singular fits explicitly unavailable. Verified: 1341 Python tests passed (15 skipped), 146 web tests passed; all gates green.

Goal. A user attaches measurements (CSV/XLSX/HDF5/MAT: a time column plus observed state columns) and asks "fit the damped oscillator to my data", or gives ODEs with unknown parameters.

What to build.

  1. Map dataset columns to the state variables, by name or an explicit mapping. Auto-detect the time column (t, time, …).
  2. Fit with scipy.optimize.least_squares, integrating with the Dynamis integrator. Support bounds, multi-start, a robust loss, and optionally fitting the initial conditions.
  3. Report:
  4. best-fit values, standard errors and 95% CIs, from cov = s²(JᵀJ)⁻¹;
  5. the correlation matrix;
  6. identifiability warnings: near-singular JᵀJ, |corr| > 0.95, or a CI wider than its value;
  7. RSS, RMSE, R² per observed variable, AIC and BIC;
  8. decimated residuals, and the fitted trajectory against the data.

Where it plugs in. - tribos/dynamis/engine.py already has dynamis_fit_parameters: extend it rather than duplicate it. - Wire tribos/agentic/fit.py to run the fit whenever a dataset is attached and a system is known. Today it says fitting is not run. - Register the tools in tribos/extensions/calibration.py and tribos/extensions/dynamis.py. - Reuse the artifact key model_calibration and upgrade web/src/components/agentic/CalibrationArtifact.tsx with: a fit-vs-data plot, a residual plot, a CI table and the warnings. - Add an evidence renderer in stem_evidence.py.

Also required by T6 and T8. Add "spec": {rhs, parameters, initial_state, t_span, method, model_name} to every dynamis_simulate_ode and dynamis_parameter_scan result. These are the exact inputs that reproduce the run.

Accept when: - Known parameters of a damped oscillator and of logistic growth are recovered from noisy synthetic data, inside their CIs. - Correlated parameters raise the warning. - Column mapping works. - spec is present on simulation results. - The agentic fit phase runs end to end with an attached dataset, using the test fakes.

docs.title: T2: PDE solver
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Added tribos/dynamis/pde/ (sparse operators; Crank-Nicolson/explicit/BDF heat, leapfrog wave, direct Poisson, method-of-lines advection-diffusion, Fisher-KPP and Burgers) with nested-grid convergence studies, Richardson estimates, exact discrete mass/energy checks, CFL refuse/adapt, the dynamis_solve_pde tool, evidence renderer and pde card. No dependencies added. Left out: 2D advection-diffusion, Fisher-KPP and Burgers (1D only, as specified), and mixed periodic/bounded 2D problems are solved without a convergence study.

Goal. Dynamis only handles ODEs. Add tribos/dynamis/pde/ (numpy/scipy only) and tribos/extensions/pde.py (tool dynamis_solve_pde, domain dynamis).

Equations, on rectangular domains: - heat/diffusion, 1D and 2D; - wave, 1D and 2D; - Poisson/Laplace, 1D and 2D; - advection-diffusion, 1D; - reaction-diffusion (Fisher-KPP), 1D; - viscous Burgers, 1D.

Boundary and initial conditions. Dirichlet, Neumann and periodic boundary conditions. Initial conditions and sources are expressions in x, y, t, parsed with safe_expr.

Methods. - Method of lines with solve_ivp, using BDF for stiff cases, or Crank-Nicolson for heat. - Central or leapfrog for wave, with a CFL check. - A sparse direct solve for Poisson. - Refuse or adapt unstable explicit settings, and report the stability number.

Verification, the core value. - A mesh-convergence study at N, 2N and (when cheap) 4N, giving the observed order p, a Richardson error estimate and a "converged" flag. - Comparison with the analytic solution when one is known. - Conservation checks: mass for periodic diffusion, energy for wave.

Output. - 1D: about 20 snapshots on the x grid. - 2D: grids of at most 80×80. - A convergence table and probe values. - Caps on grid size and wall time, set through settings.

UI. - Artifact key pde, card web/src/components/artifacts/PdeArtifact.tsx: a 1D line plot with a time slider, a 2D heatmap with a legend (theme-aware), the convergence table, and stability and verification badges. - Add an evidence renderer.

Accept when: - 1D heat matches the analytic solution with order ≈ 2. - 1D wave matches d'Alembert's solution. - A 2D manufactured Poisson problem is solved. - Mass is conserved for periodic diffusion. - A CFL violation is refused or adapted. - An unsafe expression is rejected. - The planner selects the tool for "solve the heat equation on [0,1]…".

docs.title: T3: Uncertainty propagation
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Added tribos/physis/uncertainty.py with first-order GUM and vectorised Monte Carlo propagation, Pint unit handling, CODATA autofill, a contribution budget, the physis_propagate_uncertainty tool and the uncertainty result card. No dependencies added; a compound unit is reported by its SI name ("joule") when one exists, else by its expansion. Verified: 1356 Python tests passed (15 skipped), 151 web tests passed; all gates green.

Goal. Add tribos/physis/uncertainty.py with the tool physis_propagate_uncertainty (domain physis).

Inputs. - An expression, parsed with safe_expr. - Variables {name: {value, uncertainty, unit?, distribution: normal|uniform|lognormal}}. - Optional correlations.

Methods. - linear: first-order GUM, using SymPy partial derivatives, with sensitivity coefficients and each input's percentage contribution. - monte_carlo: vectorised numpy, seedable, giving the mean, std, 95% interval and skewness. - both: runs the two and warns when they disagree, which signals nonlinearity.

Other requirements. - Units through Pint. - Optionally fill CODATA constants (c, G, h, k_B, e, m_e, N_A, …) with their uncertainties from Physis, and say so in the output. - Format the result as value ± U with k = 2: the uncertainty to 2 significant figures, and the value rounded to match. - Artifact key uncertainty, card artifacts/UncertaintyArtifact.tsx: the result, a budget table with contribution bars, and the Monte Carlo histogram.

Accept when: - Linear propagation for products and quotients adds relative uncertainties in quadrature. - Monte Carlo agrees with linear propagation for a linear function. - A nonlinear case produces the warning. - Units propagate. - CODATA autofill works.

docs.title: T4: Unit checking on every answer
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Implemented deterministic dimensional audit in tribos/verify/units_audit.py integrated into math_claims.audit_answer and VerificationNotice.tsx. Pint checks dimensional consistency, unit conversion values, and wrong unit labels; ambiguous symbols remain unevaluated. All gates and 1349 tests pass.

What to check. Extract quantity statements and equations with units from both text and LaTeX ("F = 50 N", $E = mc^2 = 9.0\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{J}$). Bind symbols to the quantities stated in the question and the answer, then check:

  • (a) dimensional consistency, using Pint (tribos/physis/units.py);
  • (b) that a stated numeric result matches its equation after unit conversion;
  • (c) wrong unit labels, for example a pressure given in N.

Unbound or ambiguous symbols are "not evaluated" and are never flagged.

Output. - Results go to verification_report.units: {checked, consistent, inconsistent: [{statement, lhs_dim, rhs_dim, reason}], not_evaluated}. - A contradiction becomes a defect that is fed back to the writer, the same way math-claim failures are. - Web: show a compact "Units: N checked, M inconsistent" line in web/src/components/VerificationNotice.tsx.

Accept when: - Wrong dimensions and wrong numeric results are caught. - Correct physics paragraphs and ambiguous symbols are not flagged. - LaTeX units (\mathrm{}, \,) are handled. - A defect is created and fed back.

docs.title: T5: Formal proof checking with Lean, optional
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Added tribos/verify/formal/ (Lean/lake discovery, temp-dir run with timeout and POSIX memory limit, diagnostics parsing, sorry/admit/axiom rejection, content-hash cache) and the model formalise-and-repair loop; the formal_proof agentic phase (after the math agent), the axiom_formal_check tool (executes_code, never replayed) and the formal_proof card. Tested with a fake Python lean. No dependencies added. Without Lean the status is "formal checker unavailable" and nothing else changes; the memory limit is not enforced on Windows; the phase runs on agentic frameworks only.

Goal. Add tribos/verify/formal/, a Lean 4 runner.

Runner. - Find lean or lake from TRIBOS_LEAN_PATH or PATH. - If TRIBOS_LEAN_PROJECT points to a Mathlib project, run lake env lean file.lean there. - Run in a temp directory with a timeout and memory limit. - Proofs containing sorry, admit or new axioms are not verified. - Cache results by content hash.

Math-agent integration (tribos/axiom/agent.py, tribos/agentic/math_agent.py). - For "prove …" questions, the LLM formalises the statement and proof, then repairs it on compiler errors up to TRIBOS_FORMAL_MAX_REPAIRS times. - Show the Lean statement next to the question, so the reader can judge whether it is faithful. - Status: - "formally verified (Lean)" only on a clean compile; - otherwise "formalisation failed" with the last error; - "formal checker unavailable" when Lean is not installed. In that case nothing else changes. - This never overrides the existing SymPy checks.

Plumbing and UI. - Tool axiom_formal_check (domain axiom), classified executes_code. - Settings: TRIBOS_LEAN_PATH, TRIBOS_LEAN_PROJECT, TRIBOS_FORMAL_TIMEOUT_S, TRIBOS_FORMAL_MAX_REPAIRS, TRIBOS_FORMAL. - Artifact key formal_proof, card artifacts/FormalProofArtifact.tsx: the Lean code with a copy button, a status badge and the compiler output.

Accept when these work, tested with a fake lean executable (a Python script that emulates success, error and sorry): - parsing compiler output; - the timeout; - rejecting sorry; - the cache; - the "unavailable" path; - math-agent integration with a fake LLM.

docs.title: T6: Interactive simulation (sliders, phase portraits, bifurcation)
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Added app/backend/routers/simulate.py (simulate, bifurcation, vector field; auth, per-user rate and concurrency limits, threaded 10 s timeout, preset fallback) over the finished interactive.py, and the web Explore panel (components/simulation/*, simulateService.ts, lib/simulationExplore.ts): debounced sliders with abort, faint original overlay and Reset, phase portrait with vector field, bifurcation tab. No dependencies added. A cards-level ApiContext passes the backend URL and auth hook to message cards; a single ODE integration cannot be interrupted, so a timed-out call keeps its user slot until it ends.

Backend: app/backend/routers/simulate.py. Add the module to the router list in main.py. Endpoints:

  • POST /api/simulate takes {model_name?, rhs?, parameters?, initial_state?, t_span, num_points<=2000, method?} and returns the dynamis_simulate_ode result shape.
  • POST /api/simulate/bifurcation takes {spec, parameter, start, stop, steps<=200, observable, transient_fraction} and returns {parameter, values, points:[{value, maxima, minima}]}.
  • Optional: POST /api/simulate/vector_field takes {spec, x_var, y_var, x_range, y_range, n<=25}.

For all endpoints: - Authenticate with get_current_user, and apply a per-user rate limit. - Run each call in a thread with a 10 s timeout. - When there is no spec (old messages), resolve model_name to a preset in ODE_PRESETS.

Web. - Add web/src/components/simulation/* and web/src/services/simulateService.ts, and extend SimulationArtifact.tsx and TrajectoryCharts.tsx. - When data.spec exists, show an "Explore" panel: - a slider and numeric input per parameter (auto range 0–2× the value, or log scale; min and max editable); - initial-condition inputs and a t_end input; - a 250 ms debounce, aborting any in-flight request; - the original run kept as a faint overlay, plus a Reset button. - Never mutate the stored message. - Phase-portrait view, with an optional vector field; a bifurcation tab. - Call through apiFetch, so a 401 raises the auth banner. Show readable messages for 429 and timeouts.

Accept when: - Endpoint shapes, caps, the timeout, auth and the preset fallback are tested. - A bifurcation diagram shows multiple maxima past the threshold (e.g. Rössler). - Web tests cover range inference, debounce and abort, and data shaping.

docs.title: T7: Read uploaded papers and reproduce them
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). PDFs upload as dataset kind paper (magic bytes, size/page caps, encrypted PDFs refused); tribos/papers/ extracts metadata, sections, equations (SymPy + LaTeX), ODEs, parameters and stated results with page and verbatim line, and reproduces claims (closed form via SymPy, ODEs via Dynamis) as reproduced / differs / not reproducible; tools archivon_read_paper, archivon_reproduce_paper, card paper_reproduction. No dependencies added. Extraction is line-based (display equations on their own line); OCR is used only when the vision OCR is installed; a stated result may serve as the input of a later equation, labelled as such.

Upload. - .pdf becomes dataset kind paper in tribos/datasets and in GET /api/datasets/limits. - Validate the magic bytes, and enforce a page cap and a size cap (TRIBOS_UPLOAD_MAX_MB_PDF, default 25). - Reject encrypted PDFs with a clear message. - Tabular-only paths (sandbox.ANALYSABLE_KINDS) must ignore papers.

Extraction: tribos/papers/. - Text per page with pypdf, plus title, authors and DOI or arXiv id, and section boundaries. - Numbered display equations, converted to SymPy where possible through safe_expr and tribos/verify/latex_math.py. - ODE systems ("dx/dt = …"). - Parameter tables ("k = 200 N/m"). - Stated numeric results ("we obtain T = 1.42 s"). - Use OCR (tribos/vision) on near-empty pages only if it is available. - Every extracted item keeps its page number and the verbatim source line.

Tools (domain archivon). - archivon_read_paper {dataset_id}. - archivon_reproduce_paper {dataset_id, targets?}. It runs Dynamis (tribos/dynamis/stated_ode.py) on each extracted ODE system and re-evaluates closed-form claims with SymPy. Each claim gets a status: - reproduced; - differs, with both values and the relative difference; - not reproducible, listing the missing parameters. - Never report "reproduced" when inputs were guessed. - Make sure attached papers reach the run as attachments.

Web. - Artifact key paper_reproduction, card artifacts/PaperArtifact.tsx: metadata, equations rendered with KaTeX, the parameter table, and the reproduction table with page references. - Accept PDFs in datasetService.ts, types/datasets.ts, DatasetLibrary.tsx and the composer attach components.

Accept when these are tested on PDFs generated with fpdf2 inside the tests: - extraction with page references; - a correct claim marked reproduced; - a wrong claim marked differs; - missing parameters marked not reproducible; - upload validation; - the limits endpoint listing .pdf.

docs.title: T8: Jupyter notebook export, and fixes to the existing exports
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Added executable nbformat-4 exports, exact ODE specs, accessible DOCX equations, LaTeX escaping/Unicode fixes, and complete web archives. No dependencies added; unsupported or incomplete historical tool replays are explicitly unavailable. Verified: 1331 Python tests passed (15 skipped), 145 web tests passed; all gates green.

Fixes first. - Known bug: Word export drops inline math ("The equation of motion is with ."). Reproduce it by POSTing a message with $...$ math to /api/export/docx through TestClient with base_url="http://localhost" and auth disabled. - Render math as native OMML in DOCX (convert the common LaTeX subset), or at minimum as a mathtext image with the LaTeX as alt text. - Make sure the PDF (fpdf2) never shows raw $\frac…. - Check the following in PDF, DOCX and MD: display math, tables containing math, code blocks, the reference list, simulation figures, Unicode (Greek, °, ±), long tables, lists. - Check that the web "Everything" zip (web/src/lib/zip.ts, exportService.ts) contains what it claims. - Check that "Copy as LaTeX" (web/src/lib/markdownToLatex.ts) compiles, escaping % & _ # and producing tabular tables. - Write one regression test per bug.

Then the notebook. - New format ipynb: POST /api/export/ipynb, included in the bundle, with an ExportMenu entry "Jupyter notebook (.ipynb)". - Build valid nbformat-4 JSON by hand, with no new dependency. Cells, in order: 1. title and metadata; 2. the question; 3. the answer as markdown; 4. per recorded tool call, a runnable cell using plain libraries: - SymPy for Axiom; - solve_ivp with the exact spec for Dynamis (from the spec added in T1, falling back to the manifest digest); - the verbatim Python code for Calcula; - constants with their uncertainty and source for Physis; 5. a plot cell; 6. a references cell; 7. a versions cell; 8. an assertion cell checking that the re-run matches the recorded values within tolerance. - Never include secrets or absolute paths.

Accept when: - The DOCX contains OMML (or images) for inline math. - The PDF text has no raw LaTeX. - The notebook JSON is valid. - The concatenated code cells run in a subprocess and reproduce a Dynamis result and an Axiom result.

docs.title: T9: Engineering calculators backed by standards and material data
docs.text:
Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Added tribos/engcalc/ (beam, column buckling, pressure vessel/UG-27, shaft, bolt, fatigue with Goodman/Gerber/Soderberg/Miner, pipe pressure drop, heat exchanger LMTD/NTU, layered wall) with Pint inputs, an 11-material table, utilisation per limit state, validity checks, GUM uncertainty, the physis_engineering_calc/physis_list_calculators tools and the engineering_calc card. No dependencies added. Uncertainty uses first-order GUM by central differences (formatted like T3) rather than T3's symbolic path, so piecewise formulas work; ASME allowables are not tabulated (S must be given).

Goal. Add tribos/engcalc/ with tools physis_engineering_calc {calculator, inputs, material?} and physis_list_calculators (domain physis).

Each calculator has: - unit-validated inputs (Pint), with optional uncertainties that flow through T3; - its formulas; - results with units; - an explicit safety factor or utilisation; - its assumptions and validity limits (for example, thin-wall only when t < r/10, and Euler only above the transition slenderness); - the reference it follows, with the section, e.g. Roark, Shigley, ASME BPVC VIII-1 UG-27, Incropera, Colebrook.

Calculators: - beam deflection and bending stress: simply supported and cantilever, under a point load and a UDL; - Euler/Johnson buckling; - thin-wall pressure vessel: hoop and longitudinal stress, and required thickness with joint efficiency; - shaft torsion, plus combined bending and torsion with von Mises; - bolt preload and torque; - fatigue: Basquin, Goodman/Gerber/Soderberg, Miner; - pipe pressure drop: Darcy-Weisbach with Colebrook/Swamee-Jain; - heat exchanger: LMTD and ε-NTU; - layered-wall conduction.

Materials. - A built-in table: S235, S355, A36, 304, 316, Al 6061-T6, Al 7075-T6, Ti-6Al-4V, copper, concrete, PEEK. - Properties: E, ν, yield, UTS, density, k, CTE, plus a source column. - Label the values as typical properties, not design allowables.

UI. Artifact key engineering_calc, card artifacts/EngineeringCalcArtifact.tsx: inputs, results, a utilisation bar, warnings and the citation.

Accept when: - Each calculator matches a textbook value (e.g. cantilever tip deflection PL³/3EI). - Validity warnings fire. - Input units are converted. - An unknown calculator returns an error. - The planner selects the tools for relevant questions.

docs.title: T10: Shared projects with review, and the ChatGPT-style sidebar
docs.text: Status: DONE (2026-10-25). Backend: members with owner/editor/viewer roles (403 vs a non-revealing 404), shared files, fact review (run facts pending, hand-added approved, rejected invalidated and never recalled), version history, a capped activity log, in-place migration of old databases, and runs that get the project's spotlighted instructions and its files (other members' read-only through membership). Web: components/sidebar/* (rail, search, projects, recency groups, row menu, profile menu, mobile drawer, persisted collapse), components/projects/* (six tabs, read-only for viewers, missing endpoints hidden, create/edit dialog) and hooks/useThreads|useProjects|useSidebarState; page.tsx shrank from 4,023 to about 3,320 lines. No dependencies added. Fact review state lives in a side table (fact_reviews) so the facts table keeps its columns; members are added by user id (there is no user directory); chats stay in the browser, so a project's chats are those on this device.

docs.title: Backend contract
docs.text:
All endpoints are under /api/projects, require auth and use JSON.

Project object: {id, name, description, instructions, icon, color, owner_id, role ("owner"|"editor"|"viewer"), member_count, fact_count, invalid_fact_count, pending_review_count, file_count, created_at, updated_at}

Projects: - POST "" with {name, description?, instructions?, icon?, color?}. - GET "" returns {projects}: both owned and shared projects. - GET /{id}, PATCH /{id} and DELETE /{id}. PATCH needs owner or editor; DELETE is owner only.

Members: - GET /{id}/members returns {members:[{user_id, role, added_at, added_by}]}. - POST /{id}/members with {user_id, role} (owner only). - PATCH /{id}/members/{user_id} with {role} (owner only). - DELETE /{id}/members/{user_id}: the owner, or members removing themselves (leaving). - Insufficient role returns 403. A non-member gets 404, which never reveals that the project exists.

Files: - GET /{id}/files returns {files:[{dataset_id, name, kind, size_bytes, added_at, added_by}]}. - POST /{id}/files with {dataset_id}. The dataset must belong to the caller. - DELETE /{id}/files/{dataset_id}. - Owner or editor only.

Memory: - GET /{id}/memory takes an optional ?review_status= filter. - Each fact gains review_status (pending|approved|rejected), reviewed_by, reviewed_at and review_note. - POST /{id}/memory with {subject, relation, object, confidence?, note?} adds a fact that starts approved. - POST /{id}/memory/{fact_id}/review with {decision: approve|reject, note?}. Rejecting a fact invalidates it. - GET /{id}/memory/{fact_id}/history returns {versions}, oldest first. - Facts written by runs start as "pending".

Activity: - GET /{id}/activity?limit=50 returns {events:[{id, at, actor, action, target_type, target_id, summary}]}. - Actions: project.created/updated, member.added/removed/role_changed, file.added/removed, fact.added/edited/invalidated/approved/rejected/deleted, run.completed.

Schema migration. Existing SQLite databases must upgrade in place, as follows: - The owner becomes a member. - Verified facts become approved, and all other facts become pending. - Cap the size of the activity log.

Runs. For a chat or job request with project_id, where the caller is a member: - inject the project's instructions as a delimited, spotlighted block of user-authored guidance; - auto-attach the project's files, in addition to any dataset_ids; - exclude rejected facts from recall.

Members may use project files owned by other members, with read-only access checked through membership. Everything else stays isolated per user.

docs.title: Web
docs.text:
Sidebar. Extract the sidebar from web/src/app/page.tsx (inline from about line 1737) into web/src/components/sidebar/*, redesigned like ChatGPT's: - brand plus a collapse toggle, collapsing to an icon rail with tooltips; - New chat; - Search chats, extending CommandPalette.tsx; - a Projects section: "New project", projects with emoji and colour, expandable to their chats, with shared projects marked; - history grouped as Today, Yesterday, Previous 7 days, Previous 30 days, then by month, with pinned chats on top; - a row "…" menu on each chat: Rename (inline), Pin, Move to project, Export, Delete (with confirmation); - a profile menu at the bottom that keeps all existing settings reachable; - a mobile drawer with a focus trap, closed with Esc; - the collapsed state persisted; - light and dark themes from the existing CSS variables; - every existing sidebar feature kept working.

Projects UI. - Chats carry thread.projectId in localStorage. Migrate existing threads unchanged. Deleting a project asks whether to keep or delete its chats. - Chats inside a project send project_id. - A project view, web/src/components/projects/*, with tabs: - Chats; - Instructions; - Files; - Memory: search, a review filter, approve/reject with a note, edit/invalidate/delete, add a fact, and a history drawer per fact; - Members; - Activity. - Viewers see a read-only version. - A create/edit dialog with an emoji picker and colour swatches. - Detect missing endpoints and hide those parts gracefully. - Move logic into hooks (web/src/hooks/useThreads.ts, useProjects.ts, …) so page.tsx gets smaller (it is about 4k lines today).

Accept when: - Backend: tests cover migration from the old schema, the role rules (403/404), members, files, review, history, activity, and the run integration (instructions in the context, files attached). - Web: tests cover recency grouping across day boundaries, pin ordering, moving chats and the migration, API error handling, and search.

docs.title: T11: Adaptive research loop, accuracy tools and thesis exports
docs.text:
Status (2026-11-02): DONE. See agentic/research-loop.md.

  • Loop. Research projects (loop mode) review the literature, write a charter, run rounds of parallel tests (CodeAct with independent replication, Lean proofs, cited literature), judge them with deterministic evidence rules, and stop when concluded or stagnant. They then write a chapter-by-chapter thesis whose numbers are checked against the ledger.
  • Accuracy tools. axiom_interval_verify, axiom_precision_check, axiom_counterexample_search, calcula_cross_validate, calcula_distribution_tests.
  • Exports. Typeset PDF (Chromium, Google Sans, KaTeX, Tribos cover), DOCX, Markdown, HTML and a reproducibility bundle.
  • Web. The research lab (ResearchLab.tsx): loop orbit, estimate, plan board, findings wall with generated UI blocks, proofs, thesis reader with exports.

Open follow-ups: - Certified-tier findings (interval or exhaustive checks wired into the test runner automatically). - A per-project choice of the sandbox time ceiling in the app.

docs.title: T12: Accuracy fixes from a failure analysis
docs.text:
Status (2026-11-06): DONE. Every wrong answer in a paired run against the base model was read in full and traced to its cause; each fix is general, never written for one problem.

  • Real-fluid properties. physis_fluid_properties (tribos/physis/fluids.py, CoolProp 8.0.0): reference equations of state for 130+ fluids; state properties, throttling (Joule-Thomson), isentropic expansion, saturation. Planned when a question names a fluid process.
  • Field conventions (tribos/agents/conventions.py): Lah numbers for "ordered subsets", bond quoting, annualised term rates with continuous discounting, the IUPAC sign of work, the textbook TCP latency model. Matched on the question's own words and passed to the writer.
  • Evidence gate. Words that narrate an exercise ("published", "according to", "a survey", "a recent graduate", "in 1976") no longer send a self-contained calculation to literature search; explicit requests still do.
  • Multiple choice. Options are found at line starts first (stem letters such as "compound B." are not options), and the options of a choose-one question are never read as requests (a simulation, a plot).
  • Claim auditor. No false "Verification found errors" banner for congruence chains, unit-prefix conversions or case lists.
  • Independent cross-check (tribos/agents/orchestration/cross_check.py, TRIBOS_CROSS_CHECK): opt-in; off by default because, measured, it overturned correct answers more often than wrong ones.

Open follow-ups: - CIP stereodescriptors from a built stereo-SMILES (needs a cheminformatics toolkit such as RDKit). - The auditor still compares "z = 0" written for a level set of a surface as a value.

docs.title: T13: Cheminformatics for structure questions
docs.text:
Status (2026-11-07): DONE, measured on the failing items only. After T12, every remaining GPQA failure in the paired run was an organic-chemistry item, and Tribos had no chemistry tooling. The clearest failure was stereodescriptors: the model had a product's geometry right and still wrote the wrong R/S labels.

  • Structure facts (physis_molecule, tribos/physis/chemistry.py, RDKit 2026.3.6):
  • formula, masses and degree of unsaturation;
  • stereocentres with CIP labels (r/s included), chiral or meso;
  • stereoisomer counts as enantiomer pairs and achiral forms;
  • distinct H and C environments;
  • the relation between two structures.
  • Descriptors to geometry (physis_stereo): a descriptor set is assigned with the CIP rules and embedded in 3D. For every ring, the tool lists which substituents share a face (cis/trans, syn/anti, endo/exo).
  • Option names to structures (tribos/physis/names.py): a parser for substituted chains and carbocycles.
  • In live runs the planner wrote unusable SMILES: it dropped substituents and left out locant numbers.
  • So, before drafting, code now builds each option's structure from its name and attaches its ring faces (presentation.option_stereo, result key chemistry). The planner is then not offered physis_stereo.
  • Numbered atoms written without hydrogens ([C:4]) are read as [CH:4], not as radicals. Every planner call in the first live run had this problem.
  • Routing: is_structure_question plans both tools. A writer note (stereodescriptor_options) tells the writer to match the mechanism's geometry to the computed faces instead of assigning R/S by hand.
  • Evidence gate: in a choose-one question, narrating words ("preliminary studies", "typically", "measured") no longer trigger literature search. Explicit requests ("cite papers", "according to") still do.

Open follow-ups:

  • Fused and bridged names: either an OPSIN-class parser or a validated model transcription. The planned tool now reports a model-written constitution's bonds by locant, and the tool description tells the planner to write atoms in locant order. A fused, bridged name still failed in 3 of 3 re-runs, because the planner's SMILES for it were invalid: a bad valence, and one locant given to two atoms. Such names need a real name parser.
  • Options given as SMILES carry no locants, so their face tables name atoms by index.
  • tests/test_audit_regressions.py::test_explicit_simulation_request_still_runs also fails on main before this change (no computed_results); not investigated here.

docs.title: T14: Chemeia, a chemistry agent
docs.text:
Status (2026-11-07): DONE, measured on GPQA's organic-chemistry items. tribos/agentic/chem_agent.py (TRIBOS_CHEM_AGENT, on by default) is an augment-stage phase for organic-chemistry questions (is_organic_question).

How a run goes:

  1. The model works the reaction as JSON: each intermediate and the target compound as SMILES (the target may be the product, a starting material or a reagent), the geometry, the chosen answer and the decisive chemistry.
  2. Code (RDKit) parses every structure and computes formulas and counts.
  3. Code matches the target to the answer options: exactly when configurations are written, otherwise by constitution. Options are built from SMILES or from their names (tribos/physis/names.py).
  4. An invalid structure, a target that matches no option, or a target that is a different option from the one chosen gets one repair round with the specific discrepancy.

The <chem_agent> evidence states that code checked the structures, not the chemistry. With the agent on, structure questions no longer force a tool plan.

docs.title: T15: Second round of fixes and enhancements
docs.text:
Status (2026-11-07): DONE.

Fixes:

  • System facts within their time limit. A named non-stiff system was checked against Radau, an implicit stiff solver. On the Lorenz system over 100 s that took 32-42 s, so the facts missed their 45 s limit under load. The second method is now LSODA, still another method family: the Lorenz facts take about 4 s, and test_explicit_simulation_request_still_runs passes again.
  • Values at named points. "At r = 0, z = 1; at r = 1, z = 0" no longer reads as a contradiction when the answer introduces the point's symbol (_AT_POINT_RE in tribos/verify/math_claims.py). A restated value that changes still fails.
  • Dependencies.
  • langchain, langchain-core and langchain-openai moved to 1.x, with the openai SDK 2.x.
  • filelock moved to 4.x.
  • safety was dropped: it capped filelock below 4, and pip-audit is the CI gate.
  • Workflows. Tribos-Alpha uses the same workflows as the public repository: newer action pins, and a Pages workflow that publishes the homepage with the documentation under /docs/.

Enhancements:

  • Molecular point groups (tribos/physis/symmetry.py):
  • the Schoenflies group of the relaxed conformer, of its heavy-atom framework, and of the most symmetric conformer within 1.5 kcal/mol;
  • reported by physis_molecule and the chemistry agent;
  • a structure without force-field parameters (hypervalent centres) gets no group rather than a wrong one.
  • Names (tribos/physis/names.py): von Baeyer bicycles (bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-2-ene), monospiro systems (spiro[4.5]decan-6-one) and skeletal replacement (7-oxa, 2-aza). Fused names remain out of scope.
  • Options given as SMILES are numbered by the canonical order of their shared constitution, so the same #k is the same atom in every option, and the centres whose labels differ are listed.
  • Majority voting for choose-one questions (TRIBOS_MC_VOTES, tribos/agents/orchestration/mc_vote.py): opt-in, off by default.
  • Public mirror sync (scripts/sync_public.py):
  • builds the public tree from main, leaving out internal material and private blocks (), and removing private changelog links;
  • checks for excluded paths, leftover private blocks and secret-looking strings;
  • commits or pushes only when asked.

Tests: tests/test_feat_round2.py.

docs.title: Configuration reference
docs.text:
Every environment variable read by tribos/ and app/ (tests excluded). Types, defaults and descriptions come from the settings registry (tribos/config/settings.py); the "Read at" column comes from scanning the code. Regenerate with python scripts/gen_env_reference.py; CI can run it with --check, which also fails when a variable read in the code is not registered. A commented template is in .env.example.

At startup the API validates the environment (tribos.config.validate_environment): unparsable or out-of-range numbers, unknown choices, non-boolean flags and TRIBOS_* names that no code reads (likely typos) are logged as warnings, counted in config_problems on /api/health, and fail startup only with TRIBOS_STRICT_CONFIG=1. Invalid values fall back to the default.

Precedence for state directories: a specific variable (TRIBOS_MEMORY_DIR, TRIBOS_RUNS_DIR, TRIBOS_UPLOAD_ROOT, TRIBOS_JOBS_DIR, TRIBOS_TOOL_CACHE_DIR) wins over TRIBOS_DATA_DIR; with neither set, every store keeps its historical location under the workspace.

243 variables.

TRIBOS_LEAN_PROJECT str `` tribos/agentic/research/manifest.pytribos/verify/formal/prove.pytribos/verify/formal/runner.py A Lean project with Mathlib; proofs are checked with lake env lean there. TRIBOS_LEAN_PROVER_MODEL str `` tribos/agentic/formal_proof.py Model for Lean proof attempts (e.g. a served Goedel-Prover); empty means the synthesis model. TRIBOS_LEMMA_LIBRARY str `` tribos/verify/formal/premises.py JSON file of kernel-checked lemmas reused as premises in later proofs; empty means data/lemma_library.json. TRIBOS_MATH_AGENT bool true tribos/agentic/math_agent.py Run the verified mathematics agent (bounded ReAct loop over the Axiom tools with an independent verifier) on mathematical questions. TRIBOS_MATH_AGENT_MAX_REPAIRS int (0 to 10) 4 tribos/axiom/agent.py Local repairs of one failed step before the agent switches strategy. TRIBOS_MATH_AGENT_MAX_STEPS int (2 to 40) 12 tribos/axiom/agent.py Tool calls one mathematics-agent run may make. TRIBOS_MATH_TRAJECTORY_DIR path unset tribos/axiom/agent.py Append every mathematics-agent trajectory here as JSONL (tool calls, observations, verification labels) for evaluation and fine-tuning data. TRIBOS_MC_VOTES int (1 to 9) 1 tribos/agents/orchestration/mc_vote.py Drafts that vote on a choose-one question's option (self-consistency); 1 is off, 3 or 5 multiply the drafting cost and keep the majority option. TRIBOS_SAGEMATH_PATH str unset tribos/axiom/sagemath.py SageMath executable, or wsl:<wsl.exe arguments> to run it inside WSL; discovered on PATH and in WSL when unset.

docs.title: TRIBOS_VISION_*: Image input (OCR and vision)
docs.text: Variable Type Default Read at Description TRIBOS_VISION bool true tribos/vision/reader.pyapp/backend/main.pyapp/backend/routers/vision.py Accept images attached to questions (POST /api/vision/read); they are read into text before the question is solved. TRIBOS_VISION_CROSSCHECK bool true tribos/vision/reader.py Read each image twice with the vision model (once from the image alone, once with the OCR drafts); readings that differ are settled by a third look at the image. TRIBOS_VISION_MAX_IMAGES int (1 to 10) 4 app/backend/main.py Images one question may carry. TRIBOS_VISION_MAX_MB int (1 to 50) 10 tribos/vision/reader.pyapp/backend/routers/vision.py Largest image upload in MB. TRIBOS_VISION_MAX_PAGES int (1 to 20) 4 tribos/vision/reader.py Pages of an attached PDF that are read (each like one image). TRIBOS_VISION_MODEL str muse-spark-1.3 tribos/vision/vlm.py Cloud vision model for remote (must be in the allowed model list). TRIBOS_VISION_OCR_MATH bool true tribos/vision/ocr.py Load Indra OCR's math models so formulas are read as LaTeX (about 60% slower OCR on math lines). TRIBOS_VISION_OLLAMA_MODEL str unset tribos/vision/vlm.py Ollama vision model for ollama (e.g. qwen2.5vl:7b); the first installed vision-family model when unset. TRIBOS_VISION_OLLAMA_URL str http://127.0.0.1:11434 tribos/vision/vlm.py Base URL of the local Ollama server. TRIBOS_VISION_PROVIDER remote | nim | ollama | ocr remote tribos/vision/vlm.py Model that corrects the OCR draft: remote (cloud, TRIBOS_VISION_MODEL; nim is its old name), ollama (local), or ocr (OCR only; the image stays on this machine). TRIBOS_VISION_TESSERACT str unset tribos/vision/tesseract.py Tesseract executable, the second text recognizer (its confident words are what a transcription is checked against); found on PATH, in Scoop or in Program Files when unset; off disables it. TRIBOS_VISION_TESSERACT_LANG str eng tribos/vision/tesseract.py Tesseract language models to read with (e.g. eng+deu); each must be installed. TRIBOS_CASSETTE_PROMPTS bool false tribos/evals/cassette.py Store full normalised prompts in recorded eval cassettes (easier miss diagnosis, larger files). docs.text: Variable Type Default Read at Description PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST str unset tribos/agentic/jobs.pytribos/agentic/router_store.pytribos/agentic/sandbox/runner.py (+8) Set by pytest; auto switches and default stores treat its presence as a test run. Never set it yourself. TRIBOS_LOAD_DOTENV bool true app/backend/main.py Load the workspace .env when the API module is imported; tests/conftest.py sets 0 so a developer .env never reaches pytest.

docs.title: Evaluating Tribos
docs.text:
Tribos — Evaluation Suites & Benchmarks Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

tribos.evals measures how well Tribos handles clinical and research questions, at three levels:

Level What runs What it checks Cost plan Question parsing and routing (build_query_context), as the orchestrator calls it Scope (research / conversational / unclear), question type, recognised entities, primary target, which sources run or are skipped Seconds. Offline needs no keys or network; --live adds the entity resolver and planner model retrieval The plan, the search plan, and the same Lithoscribe call production makes Whether the papers an expert would expect are retrieved: hit@k, recall@k, MRR About 15 s per question; EuropePMC + planner model answer The full orchestrator (or the running API with --via), in an isolated thread that is deleted afterwards Golden facts (fact recall), forbidden claims, abstention, agents run, verifier result and faithfulness, hard gates, budgets; benchmark labels; optional rubric judge 30–70 s per question on the classic pipeline, 4–20 min on agentic frameworks; full model usage

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
uv run python -m tribos.evals list                                         # suites and what they cover
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --level plan                             # offline routing check, ~5 s
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --suite clinical --level retrieval       # literature retrieval, ~2 min
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --level answer --judge                   # full answers, ~20 min
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --suite clinical --level answer --ids clin-sepsis   # one case

tribos-eval is the same command once the package is installed. Keys come from .env, as for the app.

Each run writes eval_runs/<time>_<suites>_<levels>/:

  • report.html: the summary, then every case with its checks, full answer, and what the run observed. It has a filter box (try fail).
  • report.md: the same summary, for pull requests and chat.
  • summary.json: machine-readable metrics.
  • results.jsonl: one line per case and level.
  • meta.json: model, settings, environment, and a fingerprint of the routing/retrieval code and case data.

docs.title: Suites
docs.text:
python -m tribos.evals list prints the current set.

Suite Cases Purpose math, physics, engineering 12 each Curated STEM questions across analysis, ODEs, number theory, mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics, structures, control and more, with plan, retrieval and answer expectations behavior 17 Routing, abstention, scope, safety, memory and simulation behaviour golden 5 Live only. Long questions with structured golden facts, one or more per orchestration framework stem 11 Algebra, number theory, ODEs, PDEs, proofs, simulation and an open problem math500 500 MATH-500 competition mathematics (HuggingFaceH4/MATH-500, MIT); symbolic answers gsm8k 1,319 GSM8K grade-school word problems (openai/gsm8k, MIT); numeric answers theoremqa 350+ TheoremQA across math, physics, EE and CS (MIT); numeric, boolean, choice or symbolic scibench — SciBench collegiate physics, chemistry and math numerics (MIT); numeric within 2% phybench — PHYBench symbolic physics (MIT) engdesign — Engineering analysis and design (MIT / Apache-2.0); numeric within 5% or required terms ugphysics — Undergraduate physics (CC BY-NC 4.0; needs --allow-noncommercial) gpqa 198 GPQA Diamond PhD-level science multiple choice (gated: accept the terms on Hugging Face and set HF_TOKEN) path/to/file.jsonl — Your own cases

External benchmarks are downloaded on first use and cached. Sample them with --limit 50 --seed 1; the same seed gives the same cases on every run, so two systems can be compared on an identical sample.

docs.title: Benchmarking against the base model (--system direct)
docs.text:
--system direct answers each case with the same model alone: one call with a standard benchmark prompt (reason step by step, final answer in oxed{} or as Answer: <option>), no tools, retrieval or verification. It is graded exactly as the full pipeline is, so the difference between the two runs is what the Tribos harness adds.

python -m tribos.evals run --suite math500 --level answer --limit 50 --seed 1 --system direct --out runs/direct
python -m tribos.evals run --suite math500 --level answer --limit 50 --seed 1 --system tribos --out runs/tribos

meta.json records the system. python -m tribos.evals.benchmark_report <root> pairs the two runs by case and reports accuracy with Wilson intervals, the paired difference with an exact McNemar test, Tribos's verified precision, abstention and latency, as HTML, Markdown and PDF.

docs.title: Options worth knowing
docs.text:
• --ids, --category, --tags, --limit, --seed: choose cases. --ids takes id prefixes, so clin- means every clinical case.
  • --concurrency N: answer-level cases at once (default 2). Plan and retrieval run up to 4×N.
  • --judge: score answers 1–5 on correctness, grounding, completeness, calibration and clarity against the reference answer.
  • The judge sees the verified citations, so recent papers are not mistaken for fabrications.
  • --judge-min 3.5 turns the score into a pass/fail check.
  • --judge-model uses a different model from the system under test (recommended when you can).
  • --retries N (default 1): re-runs a failed live plan or retrieval case. A pass on retry is reported as flaky, meaning an upstream service hiccup, not a regression. --answer-retries does the same for answers.
  • --resume <run dir>: continues an interrupted run, retrying only cases that errored.
  • --no-web: disables web search everywhere, to isolate the peer-reviewed path.
  • --fail-under "answer.pass_rate=0.8,retrieval.hit_rate=0.7": the run exits with code 1 below any threshold.
  • Thresholds can name any level metric: retrieval.mrr, answer.verified_rate, answer.label_accuracy, answer.judge.overall, answer.fact_recall_mean, answer.faithfulness_mean, answer.gate_pass_rate, and so on.
  • --framework <id>: runs every case with this orchestration framework (authoritative-react-compiler, agentic-plan-execute, multi-agent-supervisor, multi-agent-swarm, multi-agent-debate), overriding each case's framework.
  • --via http://127.0.0.1:8000: see Through the API.
  • --record / --replay (--replay-lenient, --cassette-dir): record answer cases to cassettes against the live system, or replay them offline. See Recorded cassettes.
  • --repeat N: runs each case N times, in sequence. The result keeps the first successful run's observations and replaces fact_recall, faithfulness, latency, calls and tokens with their means. metrics.repeat holds each run's values and the mean and SD per metric. The case passes when at least half the runs pass. It is marked flaky when runs disagree on pass/fail, or when the SD of fact_recall or faithfulness exceeds --flaky-sd (default 0.15).

docs.title: Metrics and hard gates
docs.text:
Every answer-level result reports these metrics. They are computed from stored observations, so rescore recomputes them.

Metric Meaning fact_recall Required golden facts found ÷ required facts. facts_missing lists the ids of the missing ones; optional misses are listed in facts_optional_missing faithfulness The verifier's claim audit: supported ÷ (supported + unsupported + contradicted). Claims that were not checked are excluded. RAGAS/FActScore-style steps_failed Activity steps (thoughts) with status error llm_calls, tokens_est From the agent budget (execution_artifacts.agent_run.budget.used). Agentic frameworks only; null on the classic pipeline tool_calls Tool calls in the run manifest latency_s Wall time of the question, setup turns excluded

summary.json adds, per level, by_framework (pass rate, fact recall, faithfulness, latency p50/p95 and gate failures for each requested framework) and latency_p95_s. The answer section adds fact_recall_mean, faithfulness_mean, steps_failed_mean, llm_calls_mean, tool_calls_mean, tokens_est_mean, gate_pass_rate and gate_failures.

Hard gates are deterministic required checks that run on every answer. They need no model:

  • answer.no_crash: the run returned a non-empty answer. An exception or an HTTP error from --via fails it.
  • answer.citations_in_evidence: every PMID, NCT, CHEMBL, NDA, BLA or ANDA id written in the answer appears in the run's own evidence or in the question. An id that is in neither is treated as hallucinated. The evidence comprises:
  • the canonical ids and output digests of successful tool calls;
  • the synthesis scope notes;
  • the citation entries and aliases;
  • the verifier's verified identifiers;
  • the evidence artifacts.

Model-written artifacts never count as evidence: claim confidence, the agent plan, run trace and dialogue, hypotheses and project memory. - answer.no_internal_leak: a research answer must not contain: - internal component names (Lithoscribe, Synapta, Vivarix, Lumicell, Discovery, in any case); - evidence-field keys (clinical_trials, structure_intel, total_reports, tool_status, …); - internal step ids (agent.gaps.9-12); - prompt tags ([CLINICAL_CLAIM]).

Code spans and URLs are ignored. The conversational introduction names the components on purpose, so it is not checked.

A case can switch a gate off with "skip_gates": ["answer.no_internal_leak"].

Budgets are optional per-case limits, each a required check: max_latency_s, max_tokens, max_llm_calls, max_tool_calls (0 means no tool may run, as for greetings) and min_faithfulness. A budget whose metric the run did not record, such as model calls on the classic pipeline, is reported but not failed.

docs.title: Through the API (--via)
docs.text:
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --suite golden --level answer --via http://127.0.0.1:8000 --ids golden-kras

Each answer case, and each of its setup turns, is sent to POST /api/chat with the body the web client sends: message, thread_id, enable_web_search, the case's framework, agent_options, dataset_ids and project_id, and model when --model is given. The returned JSON (the orchestrator result's to_dict()) is scored exactly like an in-process result, so the API layer is tested as well. Afterwards the thread's memory is deleted with DELETE /api/memory/thread/{id}.

Details:

  • Authentication. A bearer token is read from TRIBOS_EVAL_TOKEN. It is never written to meta.json.
  • Errors. A non-200 status, or a reply without a response string, becomes an errored result with a failed answer.no_crash.
  • Other levels. Plan and retrieval still run in-process.
  • Timeouts. Golden cases set timeout_s (1,800 s), because agentic frameworks take minutes.

docs.title: Regression control: baselines
docs.text:
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --suite golden --level answer --via http://127.0.0.1:8000
uv run python -m tribos.evals baseline save eval_runs/<run> --name golden          # eval_runs/baselines/golden.json
# ... change the system, run again ...
uv run python -m tribos.evals baseline check eval_runs/<new run> --name golden --delta 0.03
  • Saving. baseline save stores a per-case snapshot of the run. For each scored case it records pass, fact_recall, faithfulness, latency and each hard gate's outcome. Use --baseline <file> to write or read an explicit path, such as a committed baseline.
  • Checking. baseline check pairs the cases that both runs scored. For each metric (--metrics, default fact_recall,faithfulness,pass) it bootstraps a 95% CI of the mean per-case delta, new minus baseline. The bootstrap uses 2,000 resamples, a fixed seed (--seed) and pure Python.
  • When it fails. The check exits with code 1 when either holds:
  • a metric's CI upper bound is below -delta: the drop is both real and larger than the tolerance;
  • a hard gate that held in the baseline (or was not recorded there) now fails on any case.

It exits with code 2 when the baseline file does not exist. - Output. The comparison is written to <run>/baseline_check.md and baseline_check.json. It also lists cases that newly fail and cases present in only one of the two runs.

With few live cases a single bad run is noisy. Use --repeat 3 before saving a baseline or reading a drop.

docs.title: Re-scoring without re-running
docs.text:
Edited a case's expectations, or improved a scorer? Re-apply them to a finished run's stored answers, without calling the system again:

uv run python -m tribos.evals rescore eval_runs/<run>               # seconds; previous results kept in results.prev.jsonl
uv run python -m tribos.evals rescore eval_runs/<run> --rejudge     # also re-ask the judge and label grader

Retrieval results store every retrieved PMID, DOI and title in rank order, and answers store the full response and citations. Gold papers, title patterns, required facts and thresholds can therefore all change after the fact. Re-run the system only when the system itself changed.

docs.title: Comparing runs
docs.text:
uv run python -m tribos.evals compare eval_runs/<before> eval_runs/<after>

This prints metric deltas per level, every case that went from pass to fail (with the failing checks), and every case that was fixed. Run the same suites and levels before and after a change. meta.json records the code fingerprint, so you can confirm which code each run used.

docs.title: Writing a case
docs.text:
One JSON object per line. Every block is optional; a case is scored at each level it has a block for.

{"id": "clin-sepsis-criteria", "suite": "clinical", "category": "diagnosis",
 "query": "What are the diagnostic criteria for sepsis?",
 "plan": {"scope": "research", "question_type": "diagnosis", "entities": ["Sepsis"], "skip": ["vivarix"]},
 "retrieval": {"gold_pmids": ["26903338", "26903335", "26903336"],
               "gold_title_patterns": ["Sepsis-3|consensus definitions? for sepsis"], "k": 8},
 "answer": {"must_mention": ["SOFA", "lactate"], "cite_gold": true, "abstain": false},
 "reference": "Sepsis-3 defines sepsis as ... SOFA increase of 2 or more points ..."}

Guidance:

  • Gold papers. List several acceptable PMIDs (the landmark trial, its main follow-up, the guideline), each confirmed on EuropePMC. Add gold_title_patterns when any paper of the right kind is a correct result; open retrieval has many right answers. Keep patterns specific enough that an off-topic paper cannot match. Use "required": false for papers older than the 12-year citation-ranked window, or when gold is uncertain: the miss is then reported without failing the case.
  • Required facts (must_mention) are regexes; all must match, case-insensitively. Test the facts an expert would insist on, with alternatives ("IVIG|immunoglobulin"), not wording.
  • Forbidden claims (must_not_mention): fabricated figures or confirming an injected claim.
  • Abstention. "abstain": true means the answer must say the evidence or entity does not exist (hallucination traps). false adds an informational check that the answer does not open with a refusal.
  • Routing. plan.run and plan.skip name sources: synapta, lithoscribe, websurfer, vivarix, lumicell, clinical_trials, chembl, openfda, variant_intel. Set "offline": true only when the entities and routing hold without the live resolver (the offline lexicon knows common genes and drugs, not every disease).
  • Memory. setup lists earlier turns in the same thread.
  • How the case runs. framework requests an orchestration framework, and --framework overrides it. answer.framework is a different thing: the framework that must have been used, for example conversational-direct for a greeting. The case can also set agent_options (for example {"budget": {"max_llm_calls": 30}}), dataset_ids, project_id and timeout_s. Tag a case live when nothing in it can be scored offline; list shows a suite as live only when all its cases are.
  • Validation. Cases are checked on load: every regex must compile and must not contain control characters (a lost backslash turns \b into a backspace).

docs.title: Golden facts
docs.text:
Structured facts make answer correctness measurable without a judge, in the style of SAFE/FActScore. Each fact has an id and exactly one matcher:

"facts": [
  {"id": "sotorasib-nda", "pattern": "NDA\\s*#?\\s*214665"},
  {"id": "sotorasib-approval-date", "date": "2021-05-28"},
  {"id": "codebreak200-pfs-hr", "value": 0.66, "tolerance": 0.01, "ci": [0.51, 0.86], "context": "CodeBreaK|sotorasib"},
  {"id": "keynote716", "any_of": [{"id": "a", "pattern": "KEYNOTE-?716"}, {"id": "b", "pattern": "NCT03553836"}]},
  {"id": "profound-rpfs-hr", "value": 0.34, "tolerance": 0.01, "ci": [0.25, 0.47], "context": "PROfound", "required": false}
]
  • pattern is a case-insensitive regex.
  • date (ISO) also matches December 19, 2014, Dec. 19, 2014, 19 December 2014 and 12/19/2014.
  • value matches a number however it is written: 0.30, 0.3, 0·30, 1,063, a Unicode minus. A number glued to a word, as in G12C or rs121434569, never matches.
  • Use tolerance for rounding: 0.663 matches 0.66 ± 0.01.
  • With ci, an interval within window characters after the number (default 200) must also match. Any of 95% CI 0.23–0.41, (0.23 to 0.41) or 0.23, 0.41 works, with ci_tolerance defaulting to tolerance.
  • context is a regex that must occur within window characters of the match. It ties a hazard ratio to its trial.
  • any_of accepts alternative facts; any one of them counts.

Each fact is a check. An optional fact ("required": false) is informational and is left out of fact_recall. With "min_fact_recall": 0.8 in the answer block, a single answer.fact_recall check decides instead, and every fact becomes informational.

To add facts:

  1. Confirm against primary sources. Use the label or Drugs@FDA for application numbers and dates, and the trial publication or registry for hazard ratios.
  2. Check against stored runs. Run rescore on stored runs to see the facts hold on real answers before relying on them.
  3. Mark the rest optional. A fact the question does not strictly require, such as a secondary trial's HR, should be optional.

docs.title: Recorded cassettes: offline, deterministic answers
docs.text:
Live answer cases are slow and vary between runs. A cassette records every tool and model call of one answer case, so the case can be replayed offline: no keys, no network, the same result on every run. CI replays the committed cassettes on every commit.

# 1. Record locally, against the live APIs and model (in-process only; not with --via):
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --suite golden --level answer --ids golden-kras-g12c-nsclc --record
# 2. Commit the cassette: tribos/evals/cassettes/golden/golden-kras-g12c-nsclc.json
# 3. Replay (what CI does), in seconds:
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --suite golden --level answer --replay
uv run python -m tribos.evals run --suite golden --level answer --replay --repeat 2   # determinism check: never flaky

What a cassette holds (tribos/evals/cassette.py):

  • Tool calls. Each registry call is recorded with its ToolResult, keyed by the tool name and the canonical JSON of its arguments. The hook sits below the registry's argument validation and run-manifest recording, and above its cache, circuit breakers, retries and executor. A replayed run therefore still writes its own manifest, canonical ids and evidence, and the citation gate checks them as usual.
  • Model calls. Each call is keyed by the model and the prompt messages, and records the reply text and the model's reasoning. This covers models obtained through get_llm, whether called with ainvoke, astream or astream_with_reasoning: the planner, the agent phases, NLI, the synthesis, rewrites and the Reflexion correction. Replay builds no real client.
  • Side lookups. Calls made outside the registry: the BioModels search and the run manifest's upstream version probes.
  • Run settings. The case's query, setup turns and run options, the model, the web-search setting, the latency, and the registered tools.

How replay matches calls:

  • Normalised keys. Before hashing, volatile parts of prompts and arguments are replaced by placeholders: ISO timestamps, today's date (and the recording's date) in any common format, uuids, run_…/job_… ids, eval thread ids and Unix timestamps. The <retrieval_date> in a prompt does not break a replay.
  • Order. A call made several times replays its recordings in order.
  • Pinned settings. TRIBOS_NLI=llm and no tool embeddings, for recording and replay alike. Without the pin, a cross-encoder in one machine's HF cache would send that machine down a different path from CI.
  • Recorded latency. A replayed result reports the recorded run's latency (replay_latency_s holds the replay's own wall time), so its metrics match the recording.

What is stored:

  • Secrets are redacted. API keys, Authorization headers, bearer tokens, nvapi-/sk- keys, ?api_key= URL parameters and the values of *_KEY/*_TOKEN/*_SECRET environment variables never reach the file.
  • Prompts are not stored in full. Each prompt keeps a per-message hash, its length and a short preview. Set TRIBOS_CASSETTE_PROMPTS=1 while recording to keep the full normalised prompts; a miss then shows the first differing characters.
  • Size. Files larger than 2 MB are written gzipped (.json.gz).

Failures:

  • Strict by default. A call the cassette does not hold is a miss: it raises CassetteMiss, and the case fails answer.cassette even when the orchestrator recovers from the exception. The check names the call and, for a model call, which message differs from the nearest recording. run --replay exits with code 1 when any case missed.
  • Network. During replay, outbound network connections are refused and reported, so an unhooked network path shows up as a failure instead of a silent live call.
  • Stale cassettes. A case whose query, setup or run options changed since recording fails answer.cassette without running.
  • No cassette. Cases without a cassette are skipped.
  • Lenient replay. --replay-lenient answers a missed model call with the nearest recording of the same model and a missed tool call with a failed ToolResult. It reports the misses (cassette_misses) without failing, which is useful to see how far a change reaches.

When to refresh:

  • Re-record a case with --record, which overwrites its cassette, whenever its replay misses because of an intended change: a prompt, a tool argument, the search plan or the routing. Commit the new file with the change.
  • Re-record yearly. The literature search window is computed from the current year, so recordings go stale at the turn of the year.
  • Recordings capture the live services as they were. Use the live weekly golden job and baseline check to follow upstream changes; replay answers a different question: did our code change what it asks and does?

Limits:

  • Calls inside a tool are not recorded. Replay never runs the tool, so an extension tool's own model call, or a registry fallback between tools, is not stored.
  • One recording per case. --record cannot be combined with --repeat, --resume or --via.

docs.title: Continuous integration
docs.text:
.github/workflows/evals.yml has three jobs:

  • On every commit to main/master and on pull requests that touch the system or the harness, it runs the harness tests, the offline plan level and the cassette replay. None of them needs keys.
  • The plan level gates on plan.pass_rate=1.
  • The replay runs every committed cassette (run --suite <suites with cassettes> --level answer --replay) and fails on any miss. With no cassettes committed, the step is skipped with a notice.
  • Weekly and on demand, it runs retrieval and answers live, using the NVIDIA_API_KEY secret, and gates on retrieval.hit_rate and answer.pass_rate. It uploads eval_runs/ as an artifact, so the HTML report can be downloaded from the run page.
  • Weekly and on demand, golden. A third job runs the golden suite at the answer level and then checks it with baseline check --baseline tribos/evals/baselines/golden.json. When no baseline is committed, the check step is skipped with a notice. To commit one, save it from a trusted run with baseline save <run> --baseline tribos/evals/baselines/golden.json.

The push and pull-request path filters cover:

  • the agents and the agentic runtime;
  • tools, sources (including sources_extra), drug intelligence, Lithoscribe and tribos/utils/ (the model factory, HTTP helpers, biocontext);
  • the API (app/) and the harness.

docs.title: Reading results honestly
docs.text:
• A failing case is information. First check whether the expectation is right; then fix the system. The clin-crispr-screen-design case fails retrieval on purpose: literature search returns applications of CRISPR screens, not design protocols, and that weakness should stay visible.
  • Judge scores are relative. Compare them between runs with the same judge model; do not read them as absolute quality. The judge model may share blind spots with the system under test.
  • Expect variance. Live services and model sampling vary. Compare runs on the same suite, and look at flaky counts before reading a one-case change as a regression.

docs.title: Tribos Agentic System
docs.text:
Tribos — Multi-Framework Agent Architecture Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

Tribos can run each question through one of five orchestration frameworks. Choose one per request with framework, or set a default with TRIBOS_DEFAULT_FRAMEWORK. The API default is auto, which routes each question to one of the agentic frameworks (auto-routing.md).

Framework id What it does authoritative-react-compiler The classic fixed pipeline: parallel evidence, symbolic/numerical simulation, and sandboxed data analysis, then synthesis and a Reflexion audit. It runs no agentic phases. agentic-plan-execute Decomposes the question, runs an LLM-planned tool DAG in parallel (LLMCompiler), re-retrieves to fill gaps, searches for counter-evidence, checks claims with NLI and reports calibrated confidence. multi-agent-supervisor A supervisor uses a Magentic-One-style task and progress ledger to delegate to specialist agents (Archivon, Axiom, Dynamis, Calcula, Physis). multi-agent-swarm Specialist agents hand control to each other until the task is done. multi-agent-debate Gathers evidence with plan-and-execute, then critic agents debate the draft before the final answer (Du et al. 2023).
  • Verified references, agent loop and reasoning: references-agent-loop.md
  • Verified references, verification, memory, tools and data sources: references-verification-tools-data.md
  • Platform API (run control, jobs, projects, MCP, A2A): platform-api.md
  • Adaptive research loop, verification tiers, accuracy tools and thesis exports: research-loop.md
  • Reading question images (two OCR engines, cross-checked vision readings, coverage gate): image-reading.md
  • Code sandbox threat model: sandbox-security.md
  • Code sandbox operations runbook: sandbox-operations.md

docs.title: Auto routing: choosing the architecture per question
docs.text: framework: "auto" lets Tribos choose how to answer each question instead of making the user pick one of the five orchestration architectures. Auto is the default in the web app.

docs.title: Why a router, and why this one
docs.text:
The evidence on multi-agent systems says the right architecture depends on the task, and that more agents are not automatically better:
