docs.title: Azure OpenAI Deployment Guide — Tribos
docs.text:
Tribos — Biomedical Research Assistant Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

This guide provides instructions for configuring Tribos (engineered by ChronoStrider Engineering / ChronoStrider Engineering) to work with Azure OpenAI services, which is particularly useful for enterprise environments that require custom endpoints or Azure-based deployments.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Tribos supports three OpenAI deployment modes: 1. Standard OpenAI - Direct OpenAI API usage 2. Custom OpenAI Endpoint - OpenAI-compatible API with custom base URL 3. Azure OpenAI - Full Azure OpenAI service with Azure AD authentication

docs.title: For Azure OpenAI
docs.text:
• Azure subscription with OpenAI service enabled
  • Azure OpenAI resource created in Azure portal
  • Model deployed in Azure OpenAI Studio
  • Azure AD application registered for authentication

docs.title: Required Python Dependencies
docs.text: The following packages are already included in the project requirements: - langchain-openai (includes AzureChatOpenAI) - azure-identity (for Azure AD authentication)

docs.title: Option 1: Custom OpenAI Endpoint
docs.text:
If you have an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (e.g., enterprise proxy), set:

export OPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key
export OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://your-custom-endpoint.com/v1

Then select OpenAI/gpt-4o-mini models in the application dropdown.

docs.title: Option 2: Azure OpenAI with Azure AD Authentication
docs.text: For full Azure OpenAI deployment with Azure AD authentication:

docs.title: Step 1: Azure OpenAI Resource Setup
docs.text:
1. Create an Azure OpenAI resource in the Azure portal
  2. Deploy your desired model (e.g., GPT-4o-mini) in Azure OpenAI Studio
  3. Note down:
  4. Endpoint URL: https://your-resource.openai.azure.com/
  5. Deployment name: Name you gave your model deployment
  6. API Version: Recommended 2024-02-01

docs.title: Step 2: Azure AD Application Registration
docs.text:
1. Go to Azure AD App Registrations
  2. Create a new application registration
  3. Add required API permissions for Azure OpenAI:
  4. Go to "API permissions" → "Add a permission"
  5. Select "Azure Service Management" → "Delegated permissions"
  6. Add "user_impersonation" permission
  7. Create a client secret in "Certificates & secrets"
  8. Note down:
  9. Application (client) ID
  10. Directory (tenant) ID
  11. Client secret value

docs.title: Step 3: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Set the following environment variables:

# Azure OpenAI Configuration
export AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https://your-resource.openai.azure.com/
export AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT=your-deployment-name
export AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION=2024-02-01
export AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_NAME=gpt-4o-mini          # Optional: for analytics
export AZURE_OPENAI_MODEL_VERSION=1.0               # Optional: model version

# Azure AD Authentication
export AZURE_CLIENT_ID=your-application-client-id
export AZURE_TENANT_ID=your-directory-tenant-id
export AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret

# Other required APIs (unchanged)
export NVIDIA_API_KEY=your_nvidia_key
# ... other environment variables

docs.title: Step 4: Model Selection
docs.text: In the application interface, select Azure/gpt-4o-mini from the LLM dropdown to use Azure OpenAI.

docs.title: Supported Models
docs.text:
Currently supported Azure OpenAI models: - Azure/gpt-4o-mini - Maps to your Azure deployment

You can easily add more models by: 1. Adding them to the azure_openai_llms list in the Hydra config 2. Adding the mapping in streamlit_utils.py

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text:
Error: "Azure OpenAI requires AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT and AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT" - Ensure both environment variables are set correctly - Verify the endpoint URL format: https://your-resource.openai.azure.com/

Error: "Failed to create Azure token provider" - Check Azure AD application permissions - Verify client ID, tenant ID, and client secret are correct - Ensure the application has proper permissions for Azure OpenAI

Error: "Authentication failed" - Verify your Azure AD application has the required API permissions - Check if the client secret has expired - Ensure the service principal has access to the Azure OpenAI resource

docs.title: Testing Your Configuration
docs.text:
You can test Azure AD authentication manually:

from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential, get_bearer_token_provider

try:
    credential = DefaultAzureCredential()
    token_provider = get_bearer_token_provider(
        credential,
        "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default"
    )
    print("Azure authentication successful!")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Authentication failed: {e}")

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use environment variables for all sensitive information
  2. Rotate client secrets regularly in Azure AD
  3. Use managed identities when running on Azure resources
  4. Limit API permissions to minimum required scope
  5. Monitor usage in Azure OpenAI Studio

docs.title: Enterprise Deployment
docs.text:
For production deployments:

  1. Use Azure Key Vault for storing secrets
  2. Configure network access rules in Azure OpenAI
  3. Set up monitoring and logging in Azure Monitor
  4. Use managed identities instead of client secrets when possible
  5. Implement proper RBAC for Azure OpenAI resources

docs.title: Migration from Standard OpenAI
docs.text:
To migrate from standard OpenAI to Azure OpenAI:

  1. Set up Azure OpenAI resource and deployment
  2. Configure environment variables as shown above
  3. Change model selection from OpenAI/gpt-4o-mini to Azure/gpt-4o-mini
  4. Test functionality with your use cases
  5. Monitor costs and usage in Azure portal

docs.title: Cost Optimization
docs.text:
• Monitor token usage in Azure OpenAI Studio
  • Set up billing alerts in Azure
  • Consider using different model sizes based on use case complexity
  • Implement rate limiting if needed

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: SonarCloud provides advanced code quality analysis, security scanning, and technical debt tracking for the Tribos project, made by ChronoStrider Engineering (ChronoStrider Engineering). This document outlines the setup and configuration process.

docs.title: 1. SonarCloud Account Setup
docs.text:
1. Create SonarCloud Account: Go to sonarcloud.io and sign in with GitHub
  2. Import Repository: Import the AtlasRoX/TribosAI repository
  3. Generate Token: Go to Account → Security → Generate new token

docs.title: 2. GitHub Repository Configuration
docs.text:
Add the following secrets to your GitHub repository settings:

# Repository Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions
SONAR_TOKEN=your_sonarcloud_token_here

docs.title: 3. SonarCloud Project Configuration
docs.text:
The project is configured with:

  • Project Key: AtlasRoX_tribos-CS
  • Organization: atlasrox
  • Quality Gate: Uses SonarCloud's default quality gate

docs.title: 4. Analysis Configuration
docs.text: The analysis includes:

docs.title: Code Quality Metrics
docs.text:
• Code Coverage: Minimum 80% coverage required
  • Duplicated Code: Less than 3% duplication
  • Maintainability Rating: A rating required
  • Reliability Rating: A rating required
  • Security Rating: A rating required

docs.title: Security Analysis
docs.text:
• Security Hotspots: Automatic detection of security issues
  • Vulnerabilities: OWASP Top 10 compliance checking
  • Code Smells: Anti-pattern detection

docs.title: Technical Debt
docs.text:
• Maintainability: Technical debt ratio tracking
  • Code Complexity: Cyclomatic complexity analysis
  • Test Coverage: Line and branch coverage analysis

docs.title: Automatic Analysis
docs.text: The SonarCloud workflow runs on: - Pull requests to main - Pushes to main - Manual trigger via workflow_dispatch

docs.title: Current CI/CD Approach
docs.text:
• Self-contained: SonarCloud generates its own coverage, pylint, and bandit reports
  • Deterministic: One workflow produces the full analysis input set
  • No workflow cascade: Analysis no longer depends on downloading artifacts from other workflows
  • Ubuntu-only execution: SonarCloud uses one Linux job to produce consistent Python reports

docs.title: Workflow Architecture
docs.text:
PR/Push → SonarCloud Analysis
         ├─ Install uv + Python 3.12
         ├─ Generate bandit JSON for each module
         ├─ Generate pylint JSON for each module
         ├─ Run module tests with coverage XML output
         └─ Upload all reports to SonarCloud in one scan

docs.title: Workflow Triggers
docs.text:
• pull_request: Runs on PRs targeting main
  • push: Runs on changes merged to main
  • workflow_dispatch: Manual trigger for on-demand analysis

docs.title: Quality Gates
docs.text:
• Coverage is only one input
  • Security Hotspots are separate from bandit and can fail the gate independently
  • Duplication on New Code is a separate metric and is not affected by local pytest coverage

docs.title: Generated During Sonar Workflow
docs.text:
1. Coverage XML reports: One per module
  2. PyLint JSON reports: One per module
  3. Bandit JSON reports: One per module

docs.title: SonarCloud Outputs
docs.text:
1. SonarCloud Dashboard: Available on sonarcloud.io with comprehensive analysis
  2. PR Decoration: Quality gate feedback on pull requests
  3. Quality Gate Status: Pass/fail based on SonarCloud rules

docs.title: Coverage Requirements
docs.text:
• Overall Coverage: ≥ 80%
  • New Code Coverage: ≥ 90%
  • Duplicated Lines: < 3%

docs.title: Security Standards
docs.text:
• Security Rating: A (no vulnerabilities)
  • Security Hotspots: All reviewed
  • Bandit Issues: Critical issues must be resolved
  • Dependency Security: pip-audit and safety scans clean
  • File Upload Security: Streamlit uploads validated and secure

docs.title: Maintainability
docs.text:
• Maintainability Rating: A
  • Code Smells: < 10 per 1000 lines
  • Technical Debt: < 5% of total development time

docs.title: Local Analysis
docs.text:
Run SonarCloud analysis locally:

# Install SonarScanner on macOS
brew install sonar-scanner

# Run analysis
sonar-scanner \
  -Dsonar.projectKey=AtlasRoX_tribos-CS \
  -Dsonar.organization=atlasrox \
  -Dsonar.sources=tribos \
  -Dsonar.host.url=https://sonarcloud.io \

docs.title: Common Issues

  3. Check report paths in sonar-project.properties

  4. Quality Gate Failure

  5. Coverage and pylint can be green while the gate still fails on:
    • Security Hotspots

  6. Review the SonarCloud dashboard for the exact files flagged

  7. Unexpected Duplication or Hotspots

  8. Verify non-source files are excluded from SonarCloud analysis

  12. Update GitHub repository secrets

docs.title: Streamlit Security Implementation Guide — Tribos
docs.text:
Obsolete. The Streamlit applications (app/frontend/) were removed; uploads are handled by the API. See "Upload Security" in the developer guide. This page is kept for history only.

Tribos — Biomedical Research Assistant Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This document outlines the comprehensive security measures implemented for file uploads in the Tribos applications, engineered by ChronoStrider Engineering (ChronoStrider Engineering). The security implementation addresses file validation, content scanning, and protection against various attack vectors.

docs.title: Multi-Layer Validation
docs.text:
The security implementation uses a multi-layer approach:

  1. File Extension Validation - Whitelist approach for allowed file types
  2. MIME Type Verification - Detects file masquerading attacks
  3. File Size Limits - Prevents DoS attacks and resource exhaustion
  4. Content Pattern Scanning - Detects malicious content patterns
  5. Filename Sanitization - Prevents directory traversal attacks

docs.title: secure_file_upload()
docs.text:
The main security wrapper that replaces st.file_uploader():

from app.frontend.utils.streamlit_utils import secure_file_upload

# Basic usage
uploaded_file = secure_file_upload(
    "Upload Document",
    allowed_types=["pdf"],
    help_text="Upload a PDF document",
    max_size_mb=50,
    accept_multiple_files=False
)

docs.title: validate_uploaded_file()
docs.text: Comprehensive validation engine that performs: - File extension checks against whitelist - MIME type detection using python-magic - File size validation - Content pattern scanning - Security threat detection

docs.title: sanitize_filename()
docs.text: Filename sanitization to prevent: - Directory traversal attacks (../../../etc/passwd) - Dangerous characters in filenames - Overly long filenames - Reserved system names

docs.title: PDF Files
docs.text:
pdf_file = secure_file_upload(
    "Upload Research Paper",
    allowed_types=["pdf"],
    max_size_mb=50
)
- Extensions: .pdf - MIME Types: application/pdf - Content Validation: Checks for PDF header (%PDF-) - Max Size: 50MB (configurable)

docs.title: XML/SBML Files
docs.text:
model_file = secure_file_upload(
    "Upload Model File",
    allowed_types=["xml"],
    max_size_mb=25
)
- Extensions: .xml, .sbml - MIME Types: application/xml, text/xml - Content Validation: Checks for XML header (<?xml) - Max Size: 25MB (configurable)

docs.title: Spreadsheet Files
docs.text:
data_file = secure_file_upload(
    "Upload Data File",
    allowed_types=["spreadsheet"],
    max_size_mb=25
)
- Extensions: .xlsx, .xls, .csv - MIME Types: Excel/CSV MIME types - Max Size: 25MB (configurable)

docs.title: Text Files
docs.text:
text_file = secure_file_upload(
    "Upload Text Data",
    allowed_types=["text"],
    max_size_mb=10
)
- Extensions: .txt, .md - MIME Types: text/plain, text/markdown - Max Size: 10MB (configurable)

docs.title: Upload Limits
docs.text:
UPLOAD_SECURITY_CONFIG = {
    "max_file_size_mb": 50,  # Global default
    "max_filename_length": 255,
    "allowed_extensions": {
        "pdf": ["pdf"],
        "xml": ["xml", "sbml"],
        "spreadsheet": ["xlsx", "xls", "csv"],
        "text": ["txt", "md"],
    },
    "dangerous_extensions": [
        "exe", "bat", "cmd", "com", "pif", "scr", "vbs",
        "js", "jar", "app", "deb", "pkg", "dmg", "rpm",
        "msi", "dll", "sys", "drv", "sh", "bash", "ps1",
        "py", "pl", "rb", "php", "asp", "jsp"
    ]
}

docs.title: Blocked Content Patterns
docs.text:
The system automatically blocks files containing: - Script tags: <script>, javascript:, vbscript: - Server-side code: <?php>, #!/bin/ - Dangerous functions: eval(), exec(), system() - Shell commands: #!/usr/bin/, shell_exec()

Note: The pattern <% is only blocked in non-PDF files, as it's part of legitimate PDF syntax. For PDFs, only truly suspicious patterns like <% eval or <% system are blocked.

docs.title: Tribos (Combined) — T2AA4P
docs.text:
T2AA4P integrates both T2B and T2KG secure uploads via shared utilities, so no additional per-app code is needed beyond calling the helpers.

# In app/frontend/streamlit_app_tribos.py

# SBML/PDF (T2B side)
uploaded_sbml_file = streamlit_utils.get_t2b_uploaded_files(app)

# Data packages and multimodal files (T2KG side)
streamlit_utils.get_uploaded_files(cfg)

# Both helpers use secure_file_upload() under the hood.

docs.title: Vivarix - XML/SBML Upload
docs.text:
def get_t2b_uploaded_files(app):
    uploaded_sbml_file = secure_file_upload(
        "Upload an XML/SBML file",
        allowed_types=["xml"],
        help_text="Upload a QSP as an XML/SBML file",
        max_size_mb=25,
        accept_multiple_files=False,
        key="secure_sbml_upload"
    )

    article = secure_file_upload(
        "Upload an article",
        allowed_types=["pdf"],
        help_text="Upload a PDF article to ask questions.",
        max_size_mb=50,
        accept_multiple_files=False,
        key="secure_article_upload"
    )

docs.title: Synapta - Data Upload
docs.text:
def get_uploaded_files(cfg):
    data_package_files = secure_file_upload(
        "💊 Upload pre-clinical drug data",
        allowed_types=["text", "spreadsheet", "pdf"],
        help_text="Drug targets and kinetic parameters",
        max_size_mb=25,
        accept_multiple_files=True,
        key="secure_data_upload"
    )

    multimodal_files = secure_file_upload(
        "📦 Upload multimodal data package",
        allowed_types=["spreadsheet"],
        help_text="Multimodal endotype/phenotype data",
        max_size_mb=50,
        accept_multiple_files=True,
        key="secure_multimodal_upload"
    )

docs.title: 1. Pre-Upload Validation
docs.text:
• File extension whitelist check
  • File type restriction by Streamlit

docs.title: 2. Post-Upload Validation
docs.text:
validation_result = validate_uploaded_file(uploaded_file, allowed_types, max_size_mb)

if not validation_result["valid"]:
    st.error(f"❌ {uploaded_file.name}: {validation_result['error']}")
    return None

# Show warnings for suspicious but not critical issues
if validation_result["warnings"]:
    for warning in validation_result["warnings"]:
        st.warning(f"⚠️ {uploaded_file.name}: {warning}")

st.success(f"✅ {uploaded_file.name} validated successfully")

docs.title: 3. Secure Processing
docs.text:
# Sanitize filename
safe_filename = sanitize_filename(uploaded_file.name)

# Create secure temporary file
with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=f"_{safe_filename}") as f:
    f.write(uploaded_file.read())
    secure_file_path = f.name

# Process using sanitized path
process_file(secure_file_path, safe_filename)

docs.title: File Masquerading Protection
docs.text:
The system detects files that have been renamed to bypass security:

malware.exe → research_paper.pdf  ❌ BLOCKED
- File extension: .pdf (appears safe)
- MIME type: application/x-executable (actual content)
- Result: BLOCKED with warning about MIME type mismatch

docs.title: Directory Traversal Protection
docs.text:
# Dangerous filename examples (all blocked/sanitized):
"../../../etc/passwd"           → "etc_passwd"
"..\\windows\\system32\\cmd.exe" → "cmd.exe"
"/var/log/sensitive.log"        → "sensitive.log"

docs.title: Content Injection Protection
docs.text: Files containing these patterns are automatically rejected: - HTML/JavaScript: <script>alert('xss')</script> - PHP code: <?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?> - Shell commands: #!/bin/bash rm -rf / - Python code injection: eval(malicious_code)

docs.title: Size-based DoS Protection
docs.text:
# File size limits by type
PDF_MAX_SIZE = 50 * 1024 * 1024    # 50MB
XML_MAX_SIZE = 25 * 1024 * 1024    # 25MB
DATA_MAX_SIZE = 25 * 1024 * 1024   # 25MB
TEXT_MAX_SIZE = 10 * 1024 * 1024   # 10MB

docs.title: Validation Errors
docs.text:
# File too large
"File too large (75.2MB). Max: 50MB"

# Wrong file type
"File extension 'exe' not allowed. Allowed: ['pdf']"

# Dangerous content
"File contains suspicious content pattern: <script"

# MIME type mismatch (warning, not error)
"MIME type mismatch: detected 'application/x-executable', expected 'application/pdf'"

docs.title: User Feedback
docs.text: The system provides clear visual feedback: - ✅ Success: File validated and accepted - ⚠️ Warning: File accepted but with concerns - ❌ Error: File rejected with specific reason

docs.title: For Developers
docs.text:
1. Always use secure_file_upload() instead of st.file_uploader()
  2. Sanitize filenames before storing or processing
  3. Use appropriate file type restrictions - only allow what's needed
  4. Set reasonable size limits based on expected use cases
  5. Handle validation errors gracefully with user-friendly messages

docs.title: For Users
docs.text:
1. Upload only necessary file types as specified
  2. Keep file sizes reasonable (under the specified limits)
  3. Use descriptive, clean filenames without special characters
  4. Verify file content matches the extension before uploading

docs.title: Security Events
docs.text: The system logs security-related events: - File validation failures - MIME type mismatches - Suspicious content detection - Size limit violations

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Key security metrics to monitor: - Upload rejection rate - Common rejection reasons - File type distribution - Size distribution

dependencies = [
    "streamlit>=1.41.1",
    "python-magic>=0.4.27",  # MIME type detection
    # ... other dependencies

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• python-magic: Requires libmagic system library
  • Linux: sudo apt-get install libmagic1
  • macOS: brew install libmagic
  • Windows: Bundled with python-magic-bin

Important: Install libmagic before running Streamlit apps, or you'll get: 

ImportError: failed to find libmagic. Check your installation

docs.title: Security Test Cases
docs.text:
1. Valid Files: Ensure proper files are accepted
  2. File Masquerading: Test renamed malicious files
  3. Size Limits: Test files exceeding size limits
  4. Content Injection: Test files with malicious patterns
  5. Directory Traversal: Test dangerous filenames

docs.title: Example Tests
docs.text:
def test_file_validation():
    # Test valid PDF
    valid_pdf = create_test_pdf()
    result = validate_uploaded_file(valid_pdf, ["pdf"])
    assert result["valid"] == True

    # Test file masquerading
    fake_pdf = create_executable_named_pdf()
    result = validate_uploaded_file(fake_pdf, ["pdf"])
    assert len(result["warnings"]) > 0  # Should warn about MIME mismatch

    # Test size limit
    large_file = create_large_file(100 * 1024 * 1024)  # 100MB
    result = validate_uploaded_file(large_file, ["pdf"], max_size_mb=50)
    assert result["valid"] == False
    assert "File too large" in result["error"]

docs.text:

  2. Advanced Content Analysis - Deep content inspection

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
The Streamlit security implementation provides comprehensive protection against file upload attacks while maintaining usability. The multi-layer approach ensures that even if one security measure is bypassed, others will catch potential threats.

For questions or security concerns, please contact the development team or create an issue in the repository.

Security is everyone's responsibility - always validate, never trust user input! 🛡️

docs.title: Testing, Linting, and Code Coverage with UV — Tribos
docs.text:
Tribos — Biomedical Research Assistant Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

This guide covers how to run tests, perform linting, and generate code coverage reports for the Tribos project, made by ChronoStrider Engineering (ChronoStrider Engineering).

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text:
# Install dependencies (production)
uv sync --frozen

# Install with development tools
uv sync --extra dev --frozen

# Run all tests
uv run pytest

# Run tests with coverage
uv run coverage run -m pytest
uv run coverage report

# Run linting
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff check --fix .  # Auto-fix issues
uv run pylint tribos/

# Run security scanning
uv run bandit -r tribos/
uv run pip-audit

# Format code
uv run ruff format .

# Pre-commit hooks (runs all checks at once)
uv run pre-commit run --all-files

# Run individual pre-commit checks
uv run pre-commit run ruff --all-files         # Linting only
uv run pre-commit run ruff-format --all-files  # Formatting only
uv run pre-commit run bandit --all-files       # Security only
uv run pre-commit run pip-audit --all-files    # Vulnerabilities only

docs.title: 1. Install UV
docs.text:
Follow the official UV installation guide:

# macOS/Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Windows
powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

# With pip
pip install uv

docs.title: 2. Install Dependencies
docs.text:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/AtlasRoX/TribosAI
cd tribos-CS

# Sync dependencies (creates .venv; pytest, coverage, ruff and pylint are in the dev extra)
uv sync --frozen --extra dev

# Install with development dependencies (recommended)
uv sync --extra dev --frozen

docs.title: 3. System Prerequisites
docs.text:
macOS/Linux users:

# macOS
brew install libmagic

# Linux (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt-get install libmagic1

Component-Specific Coverage:

# Coverage with source specification (all components)

# Show missing lines

# Show coverage by file with line numbers

Coverage Configuration (pyproject.toml):

[tool.coverage.run]
source = ["tribos"]
omit = [
    "*/tests/*",
    "*/test_*",
    "docs/*",
    "app/*",
]

[tool.coverage.report]
exclude_lines = [
    "pragma: no cover",
    "def __repr__",
    "if self.debug:",
    "if settings.DEBUG",
    "raise AssertionError",
    "raise NotImplementedError",
    "if 0:",
    "if __name__ == .__main__.:",
    "class .*\\bProtocol\\):",
    "@(abc\\.)?abstractmethod",
]

[tool.coverage.xml]
output = "coverage.xml"

    exit 1

docs.title: GitHub Workflows Documentation — Tribos
docs.text:
Tribos — Engineering & Scientific R&D Assistant Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

This document provides a comprehensive overview of all GitHub Actions workflows in the Tribos repository, made by ChronoStrider Engineering, detailing their purpose, triggers, and functionality.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Our CI/CD pipeline uses uv for fast, deterministic dependency management across all workflows. All workflows are designed to be efficient, secure, and provide comprehensive quality assurance.

docs.title: Tests Tribos
docs.text:
File: tests_tribos.yml

Purpose: Quality gates and the offline test suite (tests/) with coverage over tribos/ and app/.

Triggers: pushes and pull requests to main/master that change tribos/**, app/**, tests/**, scripts/gen_env_reference.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock or the workflow itself; manual dispatch.

Jobs:

docs.title: 1. Code Quality Checks (Ubuntu)
docs.text:
• Blocking: ruff check --select F,E9 tribos app tests (pyflakes and syntax errors), bandit -c pyproject.toml -r tribos app --severity-level high, and python scripts/gen_env_reference.py --check (every TRIBOS_* the code reads is a registered setting, and docs/configuration.md / .env.example match the registry).
  • Report only: the full ruff rule set, pylint, and bandit at every severity (legacy findings remain).

docs.title: 2. Cross-Platform Testing Matrix
docs.text:
• Matrix: Ubuntu Latest, macOS 15, Windows Latest; Python 3.12.
  • Steps: coverage run --source=tribos,app --omit="*/tests/*" -m pytest tests/, the coverage report and XML, a coverage gate (75%; measured 79% on 2026-10-25) and the Codecov upload (Ubuntu only).
  • No keys: tests/conftest.py removes every key-like variable and blocks non-loopback network access; cases marked @pytest.mark.network run only with TRIBOS_LIVE_TESTS=1.

docs.title: Tests Scientific Validation
docs.text:
File: tests_scientific_validation.yml

Purpose: The same tests/ suite with its own coverage gate, ruff on the core packages and a report-only mypy job.

docs.title: Tests Web
docs.text:
File: tests_web.yml

Purpose: Next.js web application linting, typechecking, and unit tests with KaTeX validation.

docs.title: Evals Workflow
docs.text:
File: evals.yml

Purpose: The evaluation harness (python -m tribos.evals, see docs/evals.md). On pushes and pull requests that touch the agents, tools, specialist packages or app/: the harness tests, the offline plan gate over the math, physics, engineering and behavior suites (every offline expectation must hold) and the replay of committed answer cassettes. Weekly and on manual dispatch: live retrieval and answer levels with the rubric judge.

docs.title: Security Audit
docs.text:
File: security_audit.yml

Purpose: Focused dependency security monitoring and vulnerability detection

Triggers: - Weekly schedule (Sundays at 2 AM UTC) - Push to main affecting pyproject.toml or uv.lock - Pull requests to main affecting dependency files - Manual workflow dispatch

Jobs:

docs.title: 1. Dependency Security Scan
docs.text:
• Tools: pip-audit, safety
  • Outputs: JSON and Markdown reports
  • Features: Continues on error to allow other jobs

docs.title: 2. SARIF Upload & Processing
docs.text:
• Purpose: Integration with GitHub Security tab
  • Process:
  • Downloads all security reports
  • Processes vulnerability findings
  • Uploads consolidated reports
  • Focus: Dependency vulnerabilities only

docs.title: 3. Security Summary Generation
docs.text:
• Output: Markdown summary with vulnerability counts
  • Purpose: Weekly dependency vulnerability monitoring
  • Note: Code security handled by test workflows via bandit

docs.title: 4. SonarCloud Security Integration
docs.text:
• Trigger: Push to main branch only
  • Features:
  • Downloads security reports
  • Generates coverage for SonarCloud
  • Performs dependency-focused security analysis

Key Features: - ✅ Focused dependency vulnerability monitoring - ✅ Weekly automated security scanning schedule - ✅ Streamlined workflow for reliable security checks - ✅ Integration with GitHub Security dashboard

docs.title: SonarCloud Analysis
docs.text:
File: sonarcloud.yml

Purpose: Advanced code quality analysis and technical debt tracking

Triggers: - Push to main branch - Pull requests to main - Manual workflow dispatch

Environment Variables: 

OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
NVIDIA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.NVIDIA_API_KEY }}

Process: 1. Setup: UV dependency installation with dev dependencies 2. Report generation: Bandit and pylint JSON reports for each module 3. Testing: Ubuntu test runs with per-module coverage XML generation 4. Upload: One self-contained SonarCloud scan with all reports

Key Features: - ✅ No workflow_run dependency or artifact download cascade - ✅ Stable report generation in a single workflow - ✅ Excludes tracked non-source files like .venv, .egg-info, .env, and Dockerfiles - ✅ Sonar duplication analysis limited away from low-value boilerplate modules

docs.title: Docker Build
docs.text:
File: docker_build.yml

Purpose: Build and push the two images on a v* tag or a manual dispatch: tribos-backend (docker/backend.Dockerfile, context: the repository root) and tribos-web (docker/web.Dockerfile, context: web/). Images are pushed to the Docker Hub namespace in the DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE repository variable (default atlasrox) as <version> and latest.

docs.title: Package Build
docs.text:
File: package_build.yml

Purpose: Python package validation and testing

Triggers: - Pull requests to main with changes to: - pyproject.toml - uv.lock - tribos/** - Manual workflow dispatch

Features: - Quality Checks: the same blocking ruff (F, E9) and bandit (high severity) gates as tests_tribos.yml - Cross-Platform Testing: Ubuntu, macOS 15, Windows Latest - Package Validation: Builds wheel/sdist and tests installation - Dependency Resolution: Fixed PyArrow compatibility issues with uv

Key Features: - ✅ Compatible dependencies with pyarrow>=14.0.0 and datasets>=4.0.0 - ✅ Cross-platform virtual environment handling (Windows/Unix) - ✅ Uses latest available git tag for PR testing

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
File: release.yml

Purpose: Automated Python-first release management with semantic versioning

Triggers: - Push to main - Manual workflow dispatch

Features: - Python Semantic Release: python-semantic-release controls version bumps - Single version source: pyproject.toml - Quality Gates: the same blocking ruff (F, E9) and bandit (high severity) gates as tests_tribos.yml - PyPI Publishing: Automated package distribution - GitHub Releases: Generated from semantic-release notes - Docker publishing: Builds and pushes release-tagged images in the same workflow after a successful release

Semantic Release Convention: 

feat: new feature     → Minor version bump (1.0.0 → 1.1.0)
fix: bug fix         → Patch version bump (1.0.0 → 1.0.1)
BREAKING CHANGE:     → Major version bump (1.0.0 → 2.0.0)

Key Features: - ✅ Python semantic-release automation with conventional commits - ✅ Modern uv dependency management for fast builds - ✅ Releases are cut from main - ✅ Auto-creates tags, publishes to PyPI, uploads the wheel and sdist, and publishes the backend and web images

docs.title: MkDocs Deploy
docs.text:
File: mkdocs-deploy.yml

Purpose: Automated documentation deployment to GitHub Pages

Triggers: - Push to main branch with changes to: - docs/** - mkdocs.yml - tribos/** - pyproject.toml - Manual workflow dispatch

Features: - Modern UV Setup: Uses project dependencies instead of manual pip installs - Jupyter Integration: Notebook rendering with mkdocs-jupyter - Material Theme: Modern styling with mkdocs-material - Auto-Deploy: GitHub Pages deployment with force push - Smart Triggers: Only runs when documentation-related files change

Key Features: - ✅ Modern UV dependency management with uv sync --frozen - ✅ Uses project dependencies from pyproject.toml - ✅ Streamlined deployment process - ✅ Path-based triggers for efficient builds

Use coverage exclusions in pyproject.toml for legitimate cases 3. Check for import-time code paths not triggered in CI

docs.title: Dynamis — Numerical Simulation, Dynamical Systems & Optimization Engine
docs.text:
Tribos Dynamics Specialist Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

Dynamis (δύναμις — "power, dynamic force") is Tribos's numerical simulation and dynamical systems engine. Built on SciPy and NumPy, Dynamis simulates ordinary differential equations (ODEs), computes fixed-point equilibria and Jacobian eigenvalue stability, scans parameter continuation spaces, fits physical models to calibration data, and solves nonlinear optimization problems.

docs.title: 1. Role & Architectural Overview
docs.text:
Dynamis provides quantitative numerical verification and simulation for continuous-time dynamical systems, physical models, and nonlinear processes across engineering and physics.

flowchart TD
    SystemSpec["ODEs, Fixed Points, or Optimization Problem"] --> DynamisEngine["Dynamis Simulation Engine"]
    DynamisEngine --> ODESolver["SciPy solve_ivp (RK45, DOP853, Radau, BDF, LSODA)"]
    DynamisEngine --> EquilibriumSolver["Equilibrium & Stability (fsolve, Jacobian, Eigenvalues)"]
    DynamisEngine --> ParamScan["Parameter Continuation & Sensitivity Sweeps"]
    DynamisEngine --> Optimizer["SciPy optimize.minimize (Bounds, Constraints)"]
    DynamisEngine --> ParameterFitter["Nonlinear Least Squares Calibration (curve_fit)"]
    DynamisEngine --> RootFinder["Multivariate Root Finding (optimize.root)"]

    ODESolver --> Trajectories["State Trajectories & Summary Metrics"]
    EquilibriumSolver --> StabilityClass["Eigenvalue Classification (Nodes, Saddles, Spirals)"]
    ParameterFitter --> FitStats["Fitted Parameters, Standard Errors, RMSE & R²"]

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
1. Stiff & Non-Stiff ODE Time-Course Integration: Solves initial value problems using adaptive explicit (RK45, DOP853) and implicit/stiff solvers (Radau, BDF, LSODA).
  2. Built-in Physical & Circuit Presets: Instant access to canonical systems: harmonic_oscillator, damped_oscillator, lorenz, lotka_volterra, van_der_pol, sir, pendulum, rc_circuit, and rlc_circuit.
  3. Fixed-Point & Stability Classification: Finds equilibrium states where \(f(x^*) = 0\), evaluates the exact Jacobian matrix at the fixed point, computes complex eigenvalues, and classifies stability (stable node, unstable node, saddle point, center, stable/unstable spiral).
  4. Trajectory-Wide Parameter Sweeps: Automatically steps a physical parameter across a designated range, running complete simulations and recording final states, peaks, minima, and time-weighted means.
  5. Constrained & Unconstrained Optimization: Minimizes or maximizes multi-variable objective functions under box bounds and equality/inequality constraints via SciPy optimize.minimize.
  6. Nonlinear Least Squares Calibration: Fits constitutive model parameters to empirical observations \((x_i, y_i)\), yielding optimal coefficients, parameter covariance, standard errors, RMSE, and coefficient of determination (\(R^2\)).

docs.title: 3. Integration with Tribos Reasoning Pipeline
docs.text:
• Stage 2 Numerical Execution: Dynamis executes after Stage 1 literature/constants retrieval when questions require numerical solutions, trajectories, or parameter optimization.
  • Reflexion Numerical Auditing: Verification hooks cross-check claimed steady-state values and trajectory bounds against Dynamis numerical logs.
  • Safety Policy: Simulations exceeding 3600 seconds are rejected upfront (DURATION_OUT_OF_RANGE), and literature-only questions bypass Dynamis automatically.

docs.title: Example 1: Simulating a Van der Pol Oscillator
docs.text:
from tribos.dynamis.engine import dynamis_simulate_ode

sim = dynamis_simulate_ode(
    rhs={"x": "v", "v": "mu * (1 - x^2) * v - x"},
    initial_state={"x": 2.0, "v": 0.0},
    t_span=(0.0, 20.0),
    parameters={"mu": 1.0},
    num_points=500,
)
print("Final state:", sim["final_state"])
assert sim["verified"] is True

docs.title: Example 2: Non-Linear Least Squares Parameter Fitting
docs.text:
from tribos.dynamis.engine import dynamis_fit_parameters

fit = dynamis_fit_parameters(
    model_expr="A * sin(omega * t)",
    independent_var="t",
    param_names=["A", "omega"],
    x_data=[0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.14159],
    y_data=[0.0, 0.95, 0.28, -0.84, -0.76, 0.42, 0.0],
    initial_guess={"A": 1.0, "omega": 2.0},
)
print(f"Fitted A={fit['fitted_parameters']['A']:.2f}, omega={fit['fitted_parameters']['omega']:.2f}")
print(f"R²: {fit['r_squared']:.4f}")

docs.title: Physis — Physical Constants, Units, OEIS & Materials Reference Engine
docs.text:
Tribos Reference Specialist Made by ChronoStrider Engineering

Physis (φύσις — "nature, physical reality") is Tribos's authoritative scientific reference engine for physical constants, unit conversions, dimensional homogeneity verification, integer sequences, materials properties, and encyclopedic scientific concepts.

docs.title: 1. Role & Architectural Overview
docs.text:
Physis acts as the empirical grounding engine for Tribos, ensuring calculations and theoretical derivations are anchored in verified fundamental constants, correct physical dimensions, and established materials data.

flowchart TD
    UserQuery["User Inquiries & Derivations"] --> PhysisEngine["Physis Reference Engine"]
    PhysisEngine --> Constants["NIST CODATA 2022 (via SciPy)"]
    PhysisEngine --> Units["Dimensional Analysis & SI (via Pint)"]
    PhysisEngine --> OEIS["Integer Sequences (OEIS REST API)"]
    PhysisEngine --> Materials["Materials Project API v2 & Local Reference"]
    PhysisEngine --> Encyclopedia["Wikipedia Scientific REST API"]
    PhysisEngine --> Wolfram["Wolfram|Alpha LLM API (Keyed)"]

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
1. Exact Fundamental Physical Constants: Direct access to NIST CODATA 2022 constants (speed of light, Planck constant, gravitational constant, elementary charge, Rydberg constant, etc.) with physical units and standard uncertainties.
  2. Dimensional Analysis & Unit Conversions: Complete SI and non-SI conversion using Pint, including dimensional homogeneity checks of analytical equations (\([M^a L^b T^c I^d \Theta^e N^f J^g]\)).
  3. Integer Sequences (OEIS): Automated query of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences by A-number, term sequences, or combinatorial concepts.
  4. Materials Science Properties: Electronic, structural, and mechanical properties via Materials Project API v2 (band gaps, crystal systems, density) backed by a 25-material curated engineering reference table.
  5. Encyclopedic Grounding: Real-time retrieval of mathematical definitions, physical laws, and theorems from Wikipedia.
  6. Computational Fact Checking: Optional Wolfram|Alpha querying when TRIBOS_WOLFRAM_APPID is configured.

docs.title: physis_molecule
docs.text:
Exact structure facts for organic molecules given as SMILES, computed with RDKit (tribos/physis/chemistry.py).

  • Domain: physis
  • Adapter Type: LOCAL_COMPUTE
  • Timeout: 30.0 seconds
Field Type Required Default Description smiles list[str] Yes — One to eight structures as SMILES. Atom-map numbers may carry IUPAC locants. names list[str] No — A short name for each structure, such as the answer options. locants dict[str, str] No — Atom-map number to locant label for letter locants, e.g. {"31": "3a"}.

For each structure it returns:

  • the molecular formula, molecular weight and monoisotopic mass;
  • the degree of unsaturation;
  • the stereocentres and stereogenic double bonds with CIP labels (new CIP labeler, pseudoasymmetric r/s included);
  • whether the structure is chiral or meso;
  • the number of stereoisomers of its constitution, split into enantiomer pairs and achiral forms;
  • the number of topologically distinct H and C environments.

For each pair of structures it says whether they are identical, enantiomers, diastereomers or constitutional isomers. Environments are graph-symmetry classes, so diastereotopic CH2 protons count as one class.

It also gives the molecular point group (tribos/physis/symmetry.py):

  1. Up to 12 conformers are embedded and relaxed with MMFF (UFF when MMFF has no parameters); the lowest is kept.
  2. Candidate rotation axes and mirror planes are tested against the atoms within 0.3 Å.
  3. The Schoenflies group follows the standard decision chart.

Three groups are reported: that of the relaxed conformer, that of its heavy-atom framework, and the most symmetric one within 1.5 kcal/mol. A flexible molecule such as stilbene twists in its minimum (Ci) but is planar (C2h) close by. Structures without force-field parameters, such as hypervalent centres, get no group rather than a wrong one.

docs.title: physis_stereo
docs.text:
Translates stereodescriptor sets into 3D geometry. A model that has a product's geometry right can still write the wrong R/S labels. This tool is how Tribos avoids that.

Field Type Required Default Description smiles list[str] Yes — With descriptor_sets: one SMILES of the constitution, atoms mapped to their locants. Without: isomeric SMILES to describe. descriptor_sets list[str] No — e.g. ["(1R,2S)", "(1R,2R)"] or whole names; R/S, r/s and E/Z. locants dict[str, str] No — Atom-map number to locant label for letter locants. distance_pairs list[list[str]] No — Locant pairs whose 3D distance to report.

How it works:

  1. Each descriptor set is assigned with the CIP rules. Mismatched centres are flipped until the labels hold; if that does not settle, an exhaustive search over up to 2^12 assignments follows.
  2. The configuration is embedded in 3D (ETKDG with MMFF relaxation). The tool checks that the geometry keeps the labels.
  3. For every ring that holds two or more stereocentres, it lists the substituents on each face of the ring's mean plane, with cis/trans for each pair.

In a bridged bicycle, a substituent on the same face of the ring through both bridgeheads as the other bridge is endo to that bridge.

Both tools are planned for questions that turn on a structure: stereodescriptors in names, stereoisomers, chirality, NMR environments, molecular formulae, endo/exo (is_structure_question). The result reaches the writer as a <chemistry> evidence block.

A planner transcribing names into SMILES is unreliable. In live runs it dropped substituents and left out locant numbers. So for a choose-one question whose options are named with stereodescriptors, code builds the structures itself before drafting:

  1. tribos/physis/names.py parses each option's name into a locant-numbered structure.
  2. compute_option_stereo translates each option's descriptors into ring faces.
  3. The result is stored under the chemistry result key. The planner is then not offered physis_stereo.

Options given as SMILES are numbered by the canonical order of their shared constitution, so #k is the same atom in every option, and the centres whose labels differ are listed.

The name grammar covers substituted chains, carbocycles, von Baeyer bicycles and monospiro systems:

  • C1 to C12 parents, bicyclo[a.b.c] and spiro[a.b], with -ene/-yne locants;
  • skeletal replacement: oxa, aza, thia;
  • the suffixes -ol, -one, -amine, -thiol and -al;
  • alkyl, halo, hydroxy, alkoxy, nitro, amino, oxo and similar prefixes.

Fused ring names (such as "methanoisobenzofuran") and aromatic parents return nothing. Those are left to a planned tool call.

docs.title: Example 1: Verifying Dimensional Homogeneity of Kinetic Energy
docs.text:
from tribos.physis.engine import PhysisEngine

engine = PhysisEngine()
result = engine.convert_units(
    check_equation="0.5 * (10 kg) * (5 m / s)^2 = 125 J"
)
assert result["homogeneous"] is True

docs.title: Example 2: Looking up CODATA Constants for Quantum Hall Effect
docs.text:
from tribos.physis.engine import PhysisEngine

engine = PhysisEngine()
constants = engine.lookup_constants(query="von Klitzing")
# Returns exact value R_K = h / e^2 = 25812.80745... Ohm

docs.title: Example 3: Searching Integer Sequences
docs.text:
import asyncio
from tribos.physis.engine import PhysisEngine

async def main():
    engine = PhysisEngine()
    catalan = await engine.lookup_oeis("1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132")
    print(catalan["results"][0]["name"])  # Catalan numbers: C(n) = binomial(2n,n)/(n+1)

asyncio.run(main())
